method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently identifies hidden subgroups in Abelian groups from quantum states, with applications to learning stabilizer groups.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, but its focus is on quantum algorithms rather than the researcher's core interests in entanglement, thermodynamics, or quantum networks.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity to enable perception, thought, and action.
method: Uses maximum entropy models and renormalization group analysis on recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: Uncovers reproducible collective behaviors and demonstrates predictive power of statistical physics in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks, with applications to NP and QMA.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers who can obtain superpositions of transcripts, and previous constructions relied on strong assumptions not known from standard cryptographic assumptions.
method: The authors present a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head technique, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA in the common reference string model, with security based on the learning with errors (LWE) assumption.
result: Two new zero-knowledge protocols are obtained: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks and based on LWE.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions, advancing the theory of quantum cryptography.

title: A Robust And Modular Cesium Magneto-optical Trap Using Diverging Laser Beams
authors: Paola Luna, Kenneth Nakasone, Andrei Zhukov, Philip Wondrak, Brian P. Anderson, Benjamin F. Kanzer, Cristian D. Panda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs) are a workhorse technology for neutral-atom quantum sensing, simulation, and computing. Here, we demonstrate a MOT optimized for inertial quantum sensing and precision metrology applications. Our MOT traps [MATH] cesium (Cs) atoms in a robust, modular system that achieves stable operation through two design features: (1) we use diverging cooling laser beams to reduce unwanted reflections and (2) optical elements are mounted in a fiber-coupled, compact, and modular cage rigidly attached to the vacuum chamber. Following polarization-gradient cooling (PGC), the system produces atom samples with temperatures below 10 [MATH]K, similar to those achieved in conventional MOTs that use collimated laser beams. In addition, we observe trapping of [MATH] Cs atoms in a non-conventional MOT geometry, where the cooling laser beams are diagonal to the principal axis of the quadrupole magnetic field.
tldr: A robust and modular cesium magneto-optical trap using diverging laser beams for inertial quantum sensing and precision metrology.
motivation: To improve the robustness and modularity of MOTs for quantum sensing applications by reducing unwanted reflections and simplifying alignment.
method: Used diverging cooling laser beams to reduce reflections and mounted optical elements in a fiber-coupled, compact cage attached to the vacuum chamber.
result: Achieved atom samples below 10 µK after polarization-gradient cooling, similar to conventional MOTs, and demonstrated trapping in a non-conventional geometry.
conclusion: The design offers a robust, modular MOT suitable for field-deployable quantum sensors.

title: Exact Collective First-passage Statistics Of N Trail-interacting Walkers
authors: Paul Pineau, Julien Br\'emont, Olivier B\'enichou, Rapha\"el Voituriez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory encoded in the environment mediates interactions between active agents, from trail-following organisms to synthetic active matter depositing persistent tracks. Although such memory is known to strongly affect transport, its consequences for collective first-passage phenomena remain largely unexplored. Here we study [MATH] one-dimensional random walkers interacting through a shared trail field. We characterize the [MATH] (among [MATH]) arrival time at a fixed target, and the probability that exactly [MATH] walkers in [MATH] reach one boundary before the other. For the broad class of self-interacting walkers with a saturating response to the trail, we derive exact expressions for the corresponding persistence exponents and splitting probabilities. Strikingly, despite the strong history-dependent correlations generated by the common environment, splitting probabilities are exactly identical whether walkers explore simultaneously or one after another. This invariance breaks down for nonsaturating trail interactions. Our results follow from an exact representation of the collective trail field and establish a framework for first-passage phenomena in systems coupled through persistent environmental memory.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage statistics of random walkers interacting via a shared trail field, deriving exact expressions for persistence exponents and splitting probabilities.
motivation: Understanding collective first-passage phenomena in systems with environmental memory is important for biological and synthetic active matter, but such problems remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors analyze N one-dimensional random walkers with saturating trail interactions using an exact representation of the collective trail field to compute arrival times and splitting probabilities.
result: For saturating interactions, splitting probabilities are identical whether walkers move simultaneously or sequentially, but this invariance breaks for nonsaturating interactions.
conclusion: The work establishes a framework for first-passage phenomena in systems coupled through persistent environmental memory, revealing unexpected invariance properties.

title: Quantum Motion From Local Transition Susceptibility
authors: Jan Klaers
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize quantum motion based on the susceptibility of a quantum state to weak local state conversion. The inverse susceptibility can be interpreted as a passage speed characterizing local motion independently of probability transport. For individual WKB branches, it reproduces the magnitude of the local dispersion velocity in both propagating and evanescent regions. A relativistic extension yields a passage speed bounded by the speed of light, reaching this bound at the finite energy corresponding to the center of the mass gap, where the evanescent decay length equals the reduced Compton wavelength. This identifies the reduced Compton wavelength as the shortest stationary evanescent length scale compatible with relativistic quantum motion.
tldr: The paper characterizes quantum motion via local transition susceptibility, introducing a passage speed that is bounded by the speed of light in a relativistic extension.
motivation: To understand quantum motion from a local susceptibility perspective, independent of probability transport.
method: Defines inverse susceptibility as a passage speed, analyzes WKB branches, and extends to relativistic quantum mechanics.
result: The passage speed reproduces local dispersion velocity for WKB branches and is bounded by the speed of light, with the reduced Compton wavelength as the shortest evanescent length scale.
conclusion: The susceptibility approach provides a novel characterization of quantum motion with relativistic consistency.

title: Engineering Nanophotonic Modes Via The Radiation Continuum
authors: Francesco Pisani, Baptiste Fix, Thomas Krieguer, Alexis Jouan, Cheryl Feuillet-Palma, Isabelle Sagnes, Patrick Bouchon, Yanko Todorov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate, experimentally and theoretically, a universal mechanism for combining nanophotonic modes relying on radiative-loss-mediated couplings. For the case of two modes this mechanism leads to a BIC-type phenomenon characterized by the emergence of a high-quality factor subradiant mode. This mode is experimentally observed in the mid-infrared range, in arrays of double-metal patch antennas where the radiation loss rates are controlled by the geometry of the system. As the mechanism described here is independent of the specific nature or number of the interacting modes, it can be used to combine physically different resonating structures, without requiring fine symmetry tuning or specific modal configurations, opening new opportunities for resonance-based nanophotonic devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a universal mechanism for combining nanophotonic modes via radiative-loss-mediated couplings, leading to bound states in the continuum (BIC) with high quality factors.
motivation: To engineer high-quality factor nanophotonic modes without requiring fine symmetry tuning or specific modal configurations, enabling new resonance-based devices.
method: Experimental and theoretical demonstration using arrays of double-metal patch antennas in the mid-infrared range, where radiation loss rates are controlled by geometry.
result: Observation of a BIC-type phenomenon with a high-quality factor subradiant mode, independent of the specific nature or number of interacting modes.
conclusion: The mechanism provides a universal approach for combining physically different resonating structures, opening opportunities for nanophotonic devices.

title: Unveiling Structured Optical Coherence In Nonlinear Optics
authors: Ady Arie Zihao Pang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear optical interactions are typically driven by coherent sources. Recently, however, incoherent sources have also been shown to offer new opportunities in nonlinear optics. Here we study the effects of the source incoherence in second harmonic generation. We derive and experimentally validate an analytic expression for the far-field coherence function at the second harmonic frequency, which is a generalization of the well-known van Cittert-Zernike theorem. Unlike the linear optics case, here the results depend not only on the source spatial distribution, but also on the nonlinear structure of the crystal. We further show, by performing Young's double-slit measurement, that the coherence at the second harmonic increases as the light propagates inside the nonlinear crystal. Our results establish nonlinearity as a degree of freedom for optical coherence, opening a new research area at the interface of statistical optics and nonlinear optics.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of source incoherence in second harmonic generation, deriving a generalized van Cittert-Zernike theorem for nonlinear optics.
motivation: To understand how source coherence affects nonlinear optical processes and to explore nonlinearity as a degree of freedom for optical coherence.
method: Analytic derivation of the far-field coherence function for second harmonic generation, validated by experiments including Young's double-slit measurement.
result: The coherence at the second harmonic increases as light propagates inside the nonlinear crystal, and the result depends on the nonlinear structure of the crystal.
conclusion: Nonlinearity can be used to control optical coherence, opening a new research area at the interface of statistical optics and nonlinear optics.

title: StreamingQEC: Streaming Quantum Error Correction In Tightly Integrated Quantum-Classical Systems Via Certified Recurrence
authors: Panayiotis Christou, Shuwen Kan, Hao Wang, Ying Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a continuous hybrid quantum error correction (QEC) pipeline comprising measurement readout, syndrome transport, decoding, feedback, and control. Existing QEC simulators primarily evaluate circuits, noise models, decoders, and protocol-level outcomes. System architects, however, must also understand how these workloads contend for and queue across controller, compute, accelerator, and communication resources during protected logical execution. We introduce StreamingQEC, a system-level simulator that translates fault-tolerant logical workloads into resource-constrained streaming-QEC pipelines. An explicit discrete-event simulation provides the reference execution semantics. An automatic staged-fluid mode enables faster approximate design-space exploration, while a certified recurrence mechanism compresses repeated transitions only when their scheduling state and metric contributions match those of the explicit execution trace. We assemble a decoder-runtime dataset containing 9,998 measurements, of which 8,174 are used to fit performance profiles. Recurrence reproduces the reported explicit-simulation metrics across 35 calibrated-profile configurations, as well as additional workload and cadence validation cases. For a 16-job anchor workload, it preserves 59,743,936 decoding events while achieving a 24.0x host-side speedup, and recurrent simulations scale beyond 1.22 billion events. Across 17 reference configurations, the automatics taged-fluid mode yields a mean makespan error of 2.60% and a worst-case error of 6.45%. Design-space studies reveal transfer-limited resource matching,decoder-driven pipeline stalls, and saturation of dedicated resources under microsecond-scale QEC cycles.
tldr: StreamingQEC is a system-level simulator for streaming quantum error correction pipelines, focusing on resource contention and scheduling in hybrid quantum-classical systems.
motivation: Existing QEC simulators focus on circuits and decoders but ignore system-level resource contention, which is critical for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The paper develops a discrete-event simulator with an automatic staged-fluid mode and a certified recurrence mechanism to compress repeated transitions, validated against a decoder-runtime dataset.
result: The simulator achieves a 24.0x speedup for a 16-job anchor workload while preserving 59.7 million decoding events, and the fluid mode yields a mean makespan error of 2.60%.
conclusion: StreamingQEC enables efficient design-space exploration of QEC pipelines, revealing resource matching and decoder-driven pipeline stalls.

title: A Physics-Grounded Qubo Encoding Of Irrigation Scheduling For Qaoa
authors: Alisher Ilhamov Alisher Ortikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotational irrigation scheduling in water-scarce Central Asia is a densely coupled combinatorial problem: soil-moisture memory links each irrigation decision to all later days within a zone, field adjacency couples zones on overlapping window days, and rigid canal rotations quantize water delivery in time. We formulate it as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) by linearizing the root-zone water balance, so the quadratic crop-stress objective generates the physical couplings as 2-local Ising interactions with no higher-order terms; only the water-budget constraint requires an artificial all-to-all penalty, which we certify with an instance-adaptive weight bound an order of magnitude tighter than generic prescriptions. Every instance is built from observed data for a cotton district in Khorezm, Uzbekistan: NASA POWER meteorology, FAO-56 Penman--Monteith evapotranspiration, SoilGrids~2.0 hydraulics, measured capillary fluxes, and documented canal-rotation windows that enter as qubit-count reductions. We benchmark four tiers -- exact solvers, matched-budget heuristics, ideal-statevector quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), and noise-model plus IBM Heron execution -- and add a scaling study on soil instances up to 584 variables. Exact branch-and-bound proves optimality in seconds through 150 variables, and heuristic degradation at fixed evaluation budget is repaired by scaling the budget, so no classical scalability wall appears at deployment-relevant sizes, and none is claimed. On hardware, the informative signal is optimum-sampling enrichment over uniform sampling. We claim no quantum advantage; we deliver a physically grounded, data-complete, reproducible encoding of a societally critical scheduling problem for the quantum-utility era.
tldr: This paper formulates irrigation scheduling as a QUBO problem and benchmarks QAOA on it, but lacks a clear connection to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Rotational irrigation scheduling in water-scarce regions is a complex combinatorial optimization problem that could benefit from quantum computing.
method: The problem is encoded as a QUBO with 2-local Ising interactions, and solved using exact solvers, heuristics, and QAOA on IBM Heron hardware.
result: Exact solvers handle up to 150 variables optimally; QAOA shows optimum-sampling enrichment over uniform sampling but no quantum advantage is claimed.
conclusion: The paper provides a physically grounded encoding for a practical problem, but does not advance quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Photonic Ising Machines Toward And Beyond A Million Spins
authors: A. Aadhi, Nayem Al-Kayed, Tristan Austin, Charles St-Arnault, Nir Rotenberg, Hitesh Ballani, David V. Plant, Edwin Ng, Yoshihisa Yamamoto, Peter L. Mcmahon, Bhavin J. Shastri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combinatorial optimization problems are central to many challenges in logistics, finance, engineering, and the life sciences, yet they remain among the most computationally demanding. Many of these problems can be mapped onto the Ising model, in which binary spins interact through a network of couplings, and solutions correspond to low-energy, ideally ground-state, spin configurations. Photonic Ising machines have the potential to be fast and energy-efficient heuristic solvers of optimization problems by leveraging the low latency, high bandwidth, and inherent parallelism of optics. However, current photonic implementations remain limited in scalability, connectivity, reconfigurability, and time-to-solution, preventing their use in many practical applications. In this perspective, we examine the current landscape of photonic Ising machines, discuss the challenges and limitations of existing platforms, and identify the scientific and technological advances needed to realize large-scale systems. These developments could establish photonic Ising machines as useful hardware platforms for practical optimization.
tldr: A perspective on photonic Ising machines for combinatorial optimization, discussing scalability challenges and future advances.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems are computationally demanding; photonic Ising machines offer potential speed and energy efficiency but face scalability and connectivity limitations.
method: The paper reviews current photonic Ising machine implementations, identifies key challenges (scalability, connectivity, reconfigurability), and proposes scientific and technological advances needed for large-scale systems.
result: No new experimental or theoretical results; it is a perspective outlining the path toward million-spin photonic Ising machines.
conclusion: Photonic Ising machines could become useful hardware for practical optimization if scalability and connectivity issues are resolved.

title: Imprinting Topology On Thermal Light
authors: Tianle Chen, Kelsey Everts, Andrew Forbes, Yungui Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological structuring of light inevitably leverages on optical coherence to ensure that the imparted spatial phases are preserved, requiring highly coherent sources or coherence engineering embedded in the design. Now we show that thermal light can be spatially engineered to carry optical topologies in the form of Skyrmions. Such topologies are immune to time averaged decoherence, a fact we leverage on in reverse to create metasurface mediated incoherent topologies from a thermal source. The pristine nature of our measured Skyrmions validates the approach, while simulations reveal how coherence management in the metasurface design would further enhance the functionality. Remarkably, the generation stage inherits robustness from the topology, remaining immune to material and fabrication defects. Our work reports the first topologies from purely thermal light, opening a path to exploiting topology in ubiquitous everyday light sources.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the creation of optical Skyrmions using thermal light, showing that topological structures can be imprinted on incoherent light.
motivation: Topological structuring of light typically requires coherent sources; the authors aim to show that thermal light can also carry topologies, leveraging robustness to decoherence.
method: They use metasurface design to engineer spatial coherence and imprint Skyrmion topologies on thermal light, with simulations and experiments validating the approach.
result: Measured Skyrmions are pristine, and the generation is robust to material and fabrication defects, demonstrating the first topologies from purely thermal light.
conclusion: This work opens a path to exploiting topology in everyday light sources, with potential applications in imaging and communication.

title: Mixed-Timescale Differential Coding For Downlink Model Broadcast In Wireless Federated Learning
authors: Chung-Hsuan Hu, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In standard federated learning systems, the parameter server broadcasts the global model to the participating devices in every iteration. Motivated by the temporal correlation between consecutive global models, differential coding can be applied to global model dissemination to reduce the information magnitude, thereby enabling communication with fewer quantization bits. However, due to wireless link failures, devices may occasionally miss differential updates and consequently fail to reconstruct the global model. As a result, they either continue local training based on an outdated model or remain idle until the next full-model broadcast becomes available. To address this challenge, we propose a mixed-timescale differential coding (MTDC) scheme that performs differential coding at two different levels by adjusting the reference model. With MTDC, a device can reconstruct the latest global model between two full-model broadcasts even if it misses a differential update. We provide a convergence analysis that motivates the design of an age-aware variant of MTDC, along with a device scheduling policy to further improve communication efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MTDC schemes achieve superior learning performance compared to baseline methods under similar communication resource budgets in the presence of downlink transmission failures.
tldr: This paper proposes a mixed-timescale differential coding scheme for efficient global model broadcast in wireless federated learning, addressing communication failures.
motivation: Standard federated learning broadcasts global models every iteration, but wireless link failures can cause devices to miss updates and use outdated models, degrading performance.
method: The authors design a mixed-timescale differential coding (MTDC) scheme that uses two reference models to allow devices to reconstruct the latest global model even after missing updates, and introduce an age-aware variant with device scheduling.
result: Simulations show that MTDC achieves superior learning performance compared to baselines under similar communication budgets in the presence of downlink failures.
conclusion: MTDC effectively mitigates the impact of transmission failures in federated learning, improving communication efficiency and model accuracy.

title: Tensor-Network Finite Elements For Analytic Operator Equations
authors: Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Michael J. Landry, Chu-Liang Fu, Mingda Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator equations (OEs) underpin quantitative modeling across science and engineering. Finite-element (FE) methods discretize continuous OEs into finite-dimensional algebraic systems, whereas tensor networks (TNs) provide flexible variational representations of correlated discrete systems. Here, we develop a framework that connects FE with TN for analytic OEs. The power of this method comes from its ability to convert highly non-linear partial differential equations into linear matrix equations. In particular, we show that FE discretization induces a hierarchy of multilinear interaction tensors, through which differential, integral, nonlinear, memory, and delay equations can be expressed within a common algebraic structure. The resulting systems are reformulated as weighted-residual optimization problems over TN degrees of freedom. Matrix-product-state calculations for one-dimensional linear and nonlinear diffusion reproduce conventional solutions with controlled error while preserving continuity and Neumann boundary conditions. The framework provides a common variational language for analytic OEs and establishes a direct connection between FE numerical formalism and TN variational algorithms, offering a general foundation for TN-based and quantum-inspired approaches to solving OEs.
tldr: This paper connects finite-element methods with tensor networks to solve analytic operator equations.
motivation: Operator equations are fundamental in science and engineering, but solving them efficiently remains challenging. The authors aim to bridge finite-element discretization and tensor-network variational algorithms.
method: They show that finite-element discretization induces multilinear interaction tensors, allowing differential, integral, nonlinear, memory, and delay equations to be expressed in a common algebraic structure, then reformulated as weighted-residual optimization over tensor-network degrees of freedom.
result: Matrix-product-state calculations for 1D linear and nonlinear diffusion reproduce conventional solutions with controlled error while preserving continuity and Neumann boundary conditions.
conclusion: The framework provides a common variational language for analytic operator equations and establishes a direct connection between finite-element numerical formalism and tensor-network variational algorithms.

title: Quantum Determinants In Polynomial Time
authors: Daniel Soskin Igor Pak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an algebraic branching program of polynomial size which computes Cayley determinant of right quantum matrices. This is a rare example of an efficient computation of a noncommutative determinant, and the first such example for quantum groups. We extend the results to the [MATH]-Cayley determinant of [MATH]-right quantum matrices, as well as to their multiparameter generalization. The proofs are entirely combinatorial, as we relate Cayley, Moore and Valiant determinants using bijections/involutions on words. We then employ the celebrated determinant construction of Mahajan and Vinay (SODA'97), to obtain the results.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time algebraic branching program for computing the Cayley determinant of right quantum matrices, a noncommutative determinant.
motivation: Noncommutative determinants are generally hard to compute; the authors aim to find an efficient algorithm for a specific class of quantum matrices.
method: The authors use combinatorial bijections and involutions on words to relate Cayley, Moore, and Valiant determinants, then apply the Mahajan-Vinay determinant construction.
result: They obtain an algebraic branching program of polynomial size that computes the Cayley determinant for right quantum matrices and their multiparameter generalizations.
conclusion: This is the first efficient computation of a noncommutative determinant for quantum groups, demonstrating a rare example of tractable noncommutative determinant computation.

title: $r$-Minimal Poset Codes
authors: Yang Xu, Haibin Kan, Guangyue Han
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose and study [MATH]-minimal codes with respect to [MATH]-support, where [MATH] is a poset defined on the coordinate set of the ambient space [MATH]. [MATH]-Minimal [MATH]-codes are natural extensions of Hamming metric minimal codes that have been extensively studied in the literature. We characterize [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes in terms of the notion so called cutting [MATH]-blocking maps, which generalizes the well-known equivalence between minimal Hamming metric codes and cutting blocking sets. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for [MATH]-minimality in terms of [MATH]-weight defined on [MATH], where [MATH] is an arbitrary weight function. This leads to a generalization of the well-known Ashikhmin-Barg criterion for Hamming metric minimal codes. We then prove two existence results for [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes, both for general [MATH] and for the special case that [MATH] is a disjoint union of chains. When [MATH] is hierarchical, we characterize [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes in terms of [MATH]-minimal Hamming metric codes. Finally, we characterize cutting [MATH]-blocking sets induced by hierarchical posets with two levels, which further enables us to answer a question raised in Hyun, Kim, Wu and Yue .
tldr: This paper studies minimal codes with respect to poset metrics, generalizing Hamming metric minimal codes.
motivation: Minimal codes have applications in cryptography and coding theory; extending them to poset metrics broadens their applicability.
method: The authors characterize r-minimal poset codes using cutting r-blocking maps and generalize the Ashikhmin-Barg criterion to arbitrary weight functions.
result: They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for r-minimality, existence results for general posets and disjoint unions of chains, and a characterization for hierarchical posets.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of minimal codes to poset metrics, answering open questions and providing new constructions.

title: Evaluating Frontier Ai Agents As Autonomous Clinical Security Auditors
authors: Michael O. Eniolade
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical AI models can expose patients to harm when adversarial vulnerabilities go undetected, yet formal security auditing requires statistical expertise, specialized tools, and significant time. We present an open evaluation task, built on METR Task Standard v0.3.0, that tests whether frontier AI agents can autonomously implement a structured clinical AI security audit. Given a pre-trained clinical prediction model, a patient dataset, and written instructions, each agent must implement four attacks from pseudocode, compute a Security Posture Score covering FGSM robustness, membership inference resistance, expected calibration error, and boundary attack resistance, and write a structured JSON report in a Docker container using only a bash interface and no scaffolding code. Six variants span the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer and MIMIC-IV ICU mortality datasets across three model architectures with increasing defense strength, with reference scores from 55.60 to 90.41. We ran 54 evaluations across three frontier models, with three runs per variant. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4.1 completed all 18 runs and received perfect evaluator scores. GPT-4o completed 61 percent of runs and used about five times the per-run token count of Claude, although provider tokenization differs. Total API costs were 8 US dollars for GPT-4.1, 12 US dollars for Claude Sonnet 4.6, and 27 US dollars for GPT-4o. GPT-4o failures involved premature session termination, an aggregation error, and an empty submission file. The task, scoring infrastructure, and Wisconsin Breast Cancer assets are publicly released; MIMIC-IV variants require separate PhysioNet access.
tldr: This paper evaluates frontier AI agents on a clinical AI security auditing task, focusing on adversarial robustness and calibration.
motivation: Clinical AI models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, and formal security auditing is time-consuming and requires expertise. The authors aim to test whether AI agents can autonomously perform such audits.
method: The authors design a task where AI agents implement four attacks (FGSM, membership inference, calibration error, boundary attack) on clinical prediction models, compute a Security Posture Score, and output a JSON report in a Docker container.
result: Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4.1 completed all runs with perfect scores, while GPT-4o completed 61% of runs with failures due to session termination and errors. Total API costs ranged from $8 to $27.
conclusion: Frontier AI agents can effectively automate clinical AI security audits, but reliability and cost vary across models.

title: Ripple: An Open, AI-Formalized Lean 4 Framework For Computing With CRNs
authors: Xiang Huang Ho-Lin Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Ripple, an open, AI-formalized Lean 4 framework for the mathematics of computing real numbers with chemical reaction networks (CRNs). Ripple formalizes the full ladder of models -- the GPAC / CRN continuum and the CRN-computable reals, the large-population-protocol (LPP) compilation pipeline, and a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) layer bridged to the deterministic mean-field limit by three machine-checked versions of Kurtz's theorem, and two Turing-completeness results -- the Bournez-Graa-Pouly GPAC Turing-completeness construction and the Soloveichik-Cook-Winfree-Bruck stochastic-CRN universality theorem. The development is reliable (its core constructions are verified to depend on exactly the three Mathlib foundational axioms, with no sorry); it exposed genuine, fixable gaps in published proofs (the approximate-majority convergence argument and the LPP main theorem); and it proves new results -- a fully machine-checked construction of Ap\'ery's constant {\zeta}(3) as a CRN-computable number via its holonomic generating function, the same recipe turning the modular 1/{\pi} series of Ramanujan into a sharp open problem. The formalization was carried out predominantly by AI agents using only publicly available models, so the workflow is reproducible.
tldr: This paper presents a formal framework for computing real numbers with chemical reaction networks, verified in Lean 4 using AI-generated proofs.
motivation: To provide a reliable, machine-checked foundation for the mathematics of CRN computation and to expose gaps in existing proofs.
method: The authors formalize the GPAC/CRN continuum, LPP compilation pipeline, CTMC layer with Kurtz's theorem, and Turing-completeness results in Lean 4, using AI agents for proof generation.
result: The framework is verified with no 'sorry' and exposes fixable gaps in published proofs; it also proves new results like a construction of Apéry's constant as a CRN-computable number.
conclusion: Ripple demonstrates a reproducible workflow for formalizing computational models and highlights the potential of AI-assisted theorem proving.

title: A Proof Complexity Perspective On Effectively Zero-knowledge Proofs
authors: Jan Krajicek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ilango (FOCS 2025) invented effectively zero-knowledge proofs, a new variant of zero-knowledge. We reformulate it in the language of logic and give simple proofs (under the same assumptions as Ilango (FOCS 2025)) of its existence and of the key property defined in Ilango (FOCS 2025) that it is "indistinguishable from true" (that property is in Ilango (FOCS 2025) a part of the definition of the prover, not its consequence). Using the theory of proof complexity generators we show that the concept can be turned it into a genuinely zero-knowledge proofs, assuming a conjecture from the theory about the existence of a hard generator and allowing the parties to share a common random string.
tldr: This paper reformulates effectively zero-knowledge proofs in the language of proof complexity and shows they can be turned into genuinely zero-knowledge proofs under a conjecture.
motivation: To provide a simpler proof of existence of effectively zero-knowledge proofs and to connect the concept to proof complexity theory.
method: The author uses proof complexity generators and logical reformulation to analyze and extend Ilango's effectively zero-knowledge proofs.
result: The paper gives simple proofs of existence and the 'indistinguishable from true' property, and shows that under a conjecture about hard generators, the concept can be turned into genuinely zero-knowledge proofs.
conclusion: Effectively zero-knowledge proofs can be understood and strengthened using proof complexity, but the result depends on an unproven conjecture.

title: Multivariate Cryptography-Based Anonymous Certificate Scheme
authors: Abel C. H. Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As quantum computing technology continues to mature, the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has outlined a migration timeline for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), recommending the deprecation of certain elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) by 2030. Furthermore, privacy-sensitive application scenarios, such as vehicular communications, require the use of anonymous certificates. However, existing anonymous certificate schemes are still largely based on ECC. Therefore, this study proposes a multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme, aiming to design quantum-safe anonymous certificates suitable for privacy-sensitive application services. The proposed multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme is supported by rigorous mathematical proofs and illustrated with computational cases.
tldr: This paper proposes a multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme for quantum-safe privacy-sensitive applications.
motivation: Existing anonymous certificate schemes rely on ECC, which is vulnerable to quantum attacks; thus, quantum-safe alternatives are needed.
method: The scheme uses multivariate cryptography, supported by rigorous mathematical proofs and illustrated with computational cases.
result: The proposed scheme provides quantum-safe anonymous certificates suitable for privacy-sensitive services.
conclusion: Multivariate cryptography can effectively replace ECC in anonymous certificate schemes to achieve post-quantum security.

title: Electrons Do More Than Just Flow

method: Editorial overview of selected articles in the Focus issue.
result: Highlights different facets of electronic degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The field is shifting focus from charge transport to a wider range of electronic phenomena.

tldr: This paper experimentally observes the emergence of phase coherence in a magnon Bose-Einstein condensate, confirming a key prediction of BEC theory.

method: The authors use a magnon gas in a magnetic film and employ optical techniques to measure the phase coherence as the system transitions to a Bose-Einstein condensate.
result: They observe the incoherent magnon gas transform into a state with a macroscopic global phase, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: The experiment provides direct evidence of phase coherence emergence in a magnon BEC, advancing understanding of quantum condensation phenomena.

authors: Weiwei Yang

abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method for measuring the dynamic frequency of a laser using electro-optic frequency combs on an integrated lithium niobate platform, applied to high-precision 3D ranging.
motivation: Accurate measurement of laser frequency dynamics is crucial for applications like LiDAR and spectroscopy, but existing methods are limited in speed or precision.
method: Two electro-optic frequency combs with slightly different repetition rates are generated on a lithium niobate chip; the beat note between them tracks the frequency variation of a frequency-modulated laser.
result: The approach enables stable and high-precision 3D scene ranging, demonstrating the utility of integrated photonic combs for metrology.
conclusion: Integrated lithium niobate electro-optic combs provide a compact, high-performance solution for dynamic laser frequency measurement and ranging applications.

title: Universities Need Transparent Quantum Hardware
authors: Alex Krasnok

abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that universities should invest in transparent quantum hardware for educational purposes rather than relying solely on cloud access.
motivation: The authors believe that hands-on experience with quantum hardware is essential for students to understand the gap between ideal circuits and physical measurements, and that current cloud-based access is insufficient for deep learning.
method: The paper presents a perspective based on educational needs and the limitations of cloud-based quantum computing access, likely drawing on examples and arguments from the authors' experience.
result: The paper concludes that universities should procure teachable quantum systems that allow students to interact with the hardware directly, rather than purchasing high-performance but opaque 'showroom' machines.
conclusion: Transparent quantum hardware is necessary for effective quantum education, and universities should prioritize pedagogical value over raw performance when acquiring quantum systems.

method: The paper reviews various non-ideal effects in non-volatile memory-based synapses, their physical origins, and strategies to mitigate or exploit them.
result: It categorizes non-idealities and discusses both mitigation strategies and opportunities for new computing functionalities.
conclusion: Non-idealities in artificial synapses are a key challenge for neuromorphic computing, but they also offer opportunities for novel computing paradigms.

conclusion: Decoherence significantly alters Fermi's golden rule predictions, and the modified formula should be used when environmental effects are non-negligible.

We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of topological phonon band structures in a class of high-symmetry binary compounds of the form [MATH] [MATH], which crystallize in the face-centered cubic space group $Fm…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034307] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phonon nodal networks in cubic binary compounds using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To explore topological phonon band structures in high-symmetry binary compounds, which may have implications for thermal transport and phononics.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations to compute phonon band structures and identify nodal lines and surface states.
result: The compounds exhibit symmetry-protected phonon nodal networks and surface states, classified by topological invariants.
conclusion: These materials host novel topological phonon phases that could be exploited for phononic applications.

title: Orbital-selective Electron Correlations In high-${T}_{\mathrm{c}}$ Bilayer Nickelates: From A Global Phase Diagram To Implications For Spectroscopy
authors: Zhiguang Liao, Yiming Wang, Lei Chen, Guijing Duan, Rong Yu, And Qimiao Si
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiguang Liao, Yiming Wang, Lei Chen, Guijing Duan, Rong Yu, and Qimiao Si

Motivated by the high-temperature superconductivity observed in the bilayer nickelate [MATH] and the spectroscopic evidences of strong electron correlations in this compound, we address the role of its multiorbital electron correlations by proposing a gl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045112] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital-selective electron correlations in bilayer nickelate superconductors, proposing a global phase diagram and analyzing spectroscopic implications.
motivation: High-temperature superconductivity in bilayer nickelates has been observed, but the role of multiorbital electron correlations is not well understood.
method: The authors propose a global phase diagram based on a multiorbital Hubbard model and analyze spectroscopic properties using dynamical mean-field theory.
result: They identify orbital-selective correlations and their impact on the electronic structure and superconductivity.
conclusion: Orbital-selective correlations are crucial for understanding the physics of bilayer nickelates and may guide future experiments.

title: Imaginary Time Formalism For Causal Nonlinear Response Functions
authors: Sounak Sinha And Barry Bradlyn
abstract:
Author(s): Sounak Sinha and Barry Bradlyn

It is well established that causal linear response functions can be found by computing the much simpler imaginary-time-ordered Matsubara functions and performing an analytic continuation. This principle is the basis for much of our understanding of linear response for interacting and disordered syst…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045113] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an imaginary-time formalism for causal nonlinear response functions in condensed matter systems.
motivation: Linear response theory is well understood via Matsubara functions and analytic continuation, but a similar framework for nonlinear response is lacking.
method: The authors extend the imaginary-time formalism to nonlinear response by considering higher-order correlation functions and analytic continuation.
result: They derive a general expression for causal nonlinear response functions in terms of imaginary-time-ordered correlation functions.
conclusion: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute nonlinear response in interacting and disordered systems, analogous to the linear case.

title: Second-order Topological Insulator Induced By Compensated Altermagnetism Without Bulk Spin Splitting
authors: Lizhou Liu, Qing-Feng Sun, And Ying-Tao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lizhou Liu, Qing-Feng Sun, and Ying-Tao Zhang

We theoretically demonstrate a second-order topological insulating phase induced by compensated altermagnetism, while keeping the bulk gap unchanged, in a two-dimensional topological insulator film. By introducing a layer-resolved out-of-plane [MATH]-wave altermagnetic term with opposite signs on the t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045416] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a second-order topological insulator induced by altermagnetism in a 2D topological insulator film, without bulk spin splitting.
motivation: To explore topological phases induced by altermagnetism, a topic in condensed matter physics, without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a layer-resolved out-of-plane d-wave altermagnetic term with opposite signs on the top and bottom surfaces of a 2D topological insulator film and analyze the resulting topological phases.
result: They demonstrate a second-order topological insulating phase induced by compensated altermagnetism while keeping the bulk gap unchanged.
conclusion: The work presents a new mechanism for second-order topological insulators but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tunable Linear Polarization Of Interface Excitons At Lateral Heterojunctions
authors: M. V. Durnev And D. S. Smirnov
abstract:
Author(s): M. V. Durnev and D. S. Smirnov

We develop a theory of polarized photoluminescence (PL) of interface excitons localized at lateral heterojunctions between transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. We show that the circular selection rules governing interband optical transitions exactly at the band extrema are modified at finite …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045419] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of polarized photoluminescence from interface excitons at lateral heterojunctions of transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers.
motivation: Understanding and controlling the polarization properties of excitons in 2D materials is important for optoelectronic applications.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for interface excitons at lateral heterojunctions, calculating the photoluminescence polarization as a function of the in-plane wavevector and junction geometry.
result: They find that the circular polarization selection rules are modified at finite wavevectors, leading to tunable linear polarization of the emitted light.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering the polarization of light emission from 2D heterojunctions, which may be useful for nanophotonic devices.

title: Mott-Anderson Crossover Without Metallization In Pressurized $\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{r}}_{3}\mathrm{I}{\mathrm{r}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Xia Yin, Weicheng Guo, Miao Li, Chunlei Yang, Chengyu Li, Dong Wang, Jianbo Zhang, Yongjin Chen, Takeshi Nakagawa, Caoshun Zhang, Chunsheng Xia, Pengfei Shan, Xiaoping Yang, Sheng Meng, Jun Chang, Ho-Kwang Mao, And Yang Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Xia Yin, Weicheng Guo, Miao Li, Chunlei Yang, Chengyu Li, Dong Wang, Jianbo Zhang, Yongjin Chen, Takeshi Nakagawa, Caoshun Zhang, Chunsheng Xia, Pengfei Shan, Xiaoping Yang, Sheng Meng, Jun Chang, Ho-kwang Mao, and Yang Ding

Here, the authors use high-pressure transport, low-temperature magnetoresistance, x-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to show that Sr
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055114] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Mott-Anderson crossover in pressurized Sr3Ir2O7, showing that localization preempts metallization.
motivation: To understand how disorder and electronic correlations compete in bandwidth-tuned correlated materials, specifically whether metallization occurs when the Mott gap collapses.
method: High-pressure transport, low-temperature magnetoresistance, x-ray diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy measurements on Sr3Ir2O7.
result: Pressure collapses the activation gap near 12–17 GPa, but low-temperature conduction remains nonmetallic and follows three-dimensional variable-range hopping, indicating Anderson localization.
conclusion: Localization can preempt metallization in correlated materials, highlighting the role of disorder in suppressing conductivity even when the Mott gap closes.

title: Spin And Valley Coupled Optical Excitations In Semihydrogenated Bilayer Graphene
authors: Lei Hao And C. S. Ting
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Hao and C. S. Ting

The semihydrogenated bilayer graphene ([MATH]), which is a bilayer graphene semihydrogenated on one graphene layer, can be considered as the merging of a monolayer graphene and a semihydrogenated graphene ([MATH]) through the interlayer bon…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055115] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin and valley coupled optical excitations in semihydrogenated bilayer graphene, a condensed matter physics topic.
motivation: To understand the electronic and optical properties of semihydrogenated bilayer graphene, which may have applications in spintronics and valleytronics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and calculations based on density functional theory or tight-binding methods to analyze the band structure and optical transitions.
result: They find that spin and valley degrees of freedom are coupled in the optical excitations, leading to novel selection rules and polarization properties.
conclusion: Semihydrogenated bilayer graphene exhibits unique spin-valley coupled optical properties that could be exploited for future devices.

title: Designing Multiple Multiferroic Orders In Altermagnetic Transition Metal Oxytrihalides
authors: Chao Yang, Tao Li, Chenqiang Hua, Yao Wang, Yin Wang, And Tai Min
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Yang, Tao Li, Chenqiang Hua, Yao Wang, Yin Wang, and Tai Min

Multiferroic altermagnets, which integrate ferroelectricity with altermagnetism, provide a promising platform for realizing unconventional magnetoelectric coupling. However, the realization of multiple multiferroic orders in such systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover electrically reco…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055411] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates multiple multiferroic orders in altermagnetic transition metal oxytrihalides, focusing on magnetoelectric coupling and electronic reconstruction.
motivation: Multiferroic altermagnets offer a platform for unconventional magnetoelectric coupling, but multiple multiferroic orders remain unexplored.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis are used to study electronic reconstruction and ferroelectricity in altermagnetic oxytrihalides.
result: Electrically reversible ferroelectricity and multiple multiferroic orders are predicted in these materials.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to design multiferroic altermagnets with potential applications in spintronics and data storage.

title: Parity Anomaly And Its Transport Signatures In Three-dimensional Chiral Topological Phases
authors: Yu-Hao Wan, Yanmiao Han, Rundong Zhao, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hao Wan, Yanmiao Han, Rundong Zhao, and Qing-Feng Sun

The parity anomaly of a single massless Dirac fermion in [MATH] dimensions produces a half-quantized Hall conductance, a phenomenon recently confirmed on the surface of three-dimensional (3D) [MATH] topological insulators. Whether and how this anomaly generalizes to 3D topological phase…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055412] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the parity anomaly and its transport signatures in three-dimensional chiral topological phases, focusing on half-quantized Hall conductance on the surface of topological insulators.
motivation: The parity anomaly of a single massless Dirac fermion in 2+1 dimensions produces a half-quantized Hall conductance, recently confirmed on the surface of 3D topological insulators. The authors aim to generalize this anomaly to 3D topological phases.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the parity anomaly in 3D chiral topological phases, likely using field theory or topological band theory to derive transport signatures.
result: The paper demonstrates how the parity anomaly manifests in 3D topological phases and predicts specific transport signatures, such as half-quantized Hall conductance.
conclusion: The parity anomaly generalizes to 3D topological phases, providing a new signature for identifying chiral topological materials.

title: Interlayer Coupling Driven Stabilization And Superconductivity In Bilayer ${\mathrm{CoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Wenping Chen, Ziyun Zhang, And Feipeng Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Wenping Chen, Ziyun Zhang, and Feipeng Zheng

Interlayer coupling plays a critical role in van der Waals materials by governing lattice stability and emergent quantum phases, yet its impact on few-layer hexagonal [MATH] remains unclear. Here, using first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate monolayer and bilayer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055413] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interlayer coupling and superconductivity in bilayer CoTe2 using first-principles calculations.
motivation: The impact of interlayer coupling on few-layer hexagonal CoTe2 is unclear, and understanding it could reveal emergent quantum phases.
method: First-principles calculations are used to systematically investigate monolayer and bilayer CoTe2, focusing on lattice stability and electronic properties.
result: Interlayer coupling stabilizes the bilayer structure and induces superconductivity.
conclusion: Interlayer coupling is crucial for stabilizing bilayer CoTe2 and enabling its superconducting phase.

title: Holographic Aspects Of Dynamical Mean-field Theory
authors: Kouichi Okunishi And Akihisa Koga
abstract:
Author(s): Kouichi Okunishi and Akihisa Koga

Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) is one of the most standard theoretical frameworks for addressing strongly correlated electron systems. In this study, we explore a holographic renormalization-group (RG)-like structure inherent in DMFT, which we refer to as “AdS/DMFT,” by focusing on the backgroun…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065114] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores a holographic renormalization-group-like structure in dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for strongly correlated electron systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between DMFT and holographic duality (AdS/CFT) and to develop a new perspective on strongly correlated systems.
method: The authors analyze the background structure of DMFT and draw analogies with the holographic renormalization group, proposing an 'AdS/DMFT' correspondence.
result: They identify a holographic RG-like structure inherent in DMFT, suggesting a duality between DMFT and a gravitational theory in one higher dimension.
conclusion: The work provides a conceptual bridge between condensed matter theory and holography, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fragility Of Local Moments Against Hybridization With Flat Bands
authors: Max Fischer, Arianna Poli, Lorenzo Crippa, Dumitru Călugăru, Sergio Ciuchi, Matthias Vojta, Alessandro Toschi, And Giorgio Sangiovanni
abstract:
Author(s): Max Fischer, Arianna Poli, Lorenzo Crippa, Dumitru Călugăru, Sergio Ciuchi, Matthias Vojta, Alessandro Toschi, and Giorgio Sangiovanni

The Kondo screening of a localized magnetic moment crucially depends on the spectral properties of the electronic bath to which it is coupled. Unlike textbook examples, realistic systems as well as dynamical mean-field theory of correlated lattice models force us to consider sharp features in the hy…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065115] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo screening of local magnetic moments coupled to flat-band electronic baths, focusing on the fragility of local moments due to hybridization with flat bands.
motivation: Understanding how sharp features in the electronic density of states, such as flat bands, affect Kondo screening is important for correlated lattice models and realistic materials.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods, likely including dynamical mean-field theory or impurity solvers, to analyze the Kondo model with a flat-band bath.
result: They find that local moments are fragile against hybridization with flat bands, leading to suppressed Kondo screening or altered screening behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between flat bands and Kondo physics, relevant for strongly correlated electron systems.

title: Spin-valley Matching Mechanisms In High-performance Multiferroic Tunnel Junctions
authors: Zhi Yang, Bao-Fu Ruan, Min Li, Bing-Xin Liu, Chuan-Kui Wang, Zong-Liang Li, And Shuai Qiu
abstract:
