title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding magnetic phenomena in 2D materials and their potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to unify dynamical evolution via space-time duality.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, leads to solvable models using brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of the space-time duality approach and its relationship with quantum computation, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a unified view of quantum many-body dynamics, but the paper is a review without novel contributions.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a platform for realizing novel electronic states driven by frustration and interference.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified field-theoretic framework is lacking.
method: The authors review and unify various field-theoretic approaches (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They demonstrate how these methods can be applied to chemical systems and extended to ecology and epidemiology.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying framework for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Recent observations have improved constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, but the equation of state at supranuclear densities remains uncertain.
conclusion: Future observations, especially from gravitational-wave detectors and X-ray telescopes, will further refine our understanding of dense matter.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances and open questions in spin-glass dynamics.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to benefit from interdisciplinary approaches, with future opportunities in both fundamental and applied contexts.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
result: The review summarizes the current state of theoretical methods for internal conversion and provides an outlook for future research directions.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are well-developed but need further integration into practical applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion dynamics, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel technologies, but the field is still developing and many open questions remain.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, the paper surveys spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques.
result: The review compiles current theoretical predictions and experimental constraints on spin-dependent exotic interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential connections to dark matter and dark energy, but no definitive evidence has been found.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental limits, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of circumstances where measured properties exceed classical bounds and identifies which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, homogeneity) are violated.
result: It shows that apparent violations arise from measurement conditions that violate assumptions, and that materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
conclusion: The findings clarify the limits of classical thermodynamic bounds and provide a framework for developing materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing nonstandard geometries in synthetic quantum matter.
result: Summarizes progress in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional simulations across platforms.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics in geometries not naturally available.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems serve as interfaces to probe quantum gravity effects, but conclusive results are pending.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and relates it to broader foundational puzzles.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other foundational problems.
method: The authors construct classical thought experiments that mimic extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the underlying issue appears in cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context beyond quantum foundations, addressing problems where predictions cannot be intersubjectively verified.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: This paper presents PyOpticL, an open-source Python library for modular optical layout, and demonstrates its use for building a laser system for trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical design in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and scalability.
method: The authors developed PyOpticL, a code-to-CAD optical layout tool that uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing, and created modular drop-in baseplates for common optical subsystems. They demonstrated the system with a strontium trapped-ion setup.
result: The modular optical system enabled laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates using 3D-printed baseplates.
conclusion: PyOpticL enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design for quantum computing and AMO physics.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions for highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and magnetometry applications.
motivation: To understand and model the previously unexplored alignment tensor contributions in metastability-exchange optical pumping at high polarization, which affect relaxation and frequency shifts.
method: A linearized mean-field model is developed and validated through free-induction-decay measurements on ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles.
result: Pronounced dependence of the ensemble response on nuclear polarization is observed, and the model shows good agreement with experiment.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Strain-driven Transition From Correlated Insulating To Semimetallic States In Twisted-bilayer Graphene
authors: Lishuai Guo, Abulimiti Yasen, Mei Xiang, Wenliang Zhu And Minghu Pan
abstract: We investigate the interplay between Coulomb interaction and uniaxial heterostrain in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) using a self-consistent Hartree–Fock (HF) approach projected onto the flat bands. For integer filling factors in the range of , we find that heterostrain strongly reconstructs the low-energy band structure and suppresses interaction-induced insulating gaps. As strain magnitude increases, the flat-band bandwidth is substantially enhanced, leading to an increased kinetic energy. The bandwidth enhancement effectively weakens the interaction strength relative to kinetic energy, resulting in the suppression of HF gaps and the emergence of semimetallic (SM) states. The strain effect can be primarily controlled by the filling factor, as well as the strain direction. At moderate strain strengths around 0.3% for , it can drive transitions between correlated insulating and SM states. In contrast, for , the HF gaps becomes negligible and the system remains essentially SM; both the strain direction and magnitude have negligible influence. Our results demonstrate that uniaxial heterostrain serves as an effective and versatile parameter for tuning correlated phases in TBG through the interplay of lattice deformation and Coulomb interactions.
tldr: This paper studies strain-driven transitions between correlated insulating and semimetallic states in twisted bilayer graphene using Hartree-Fock calculations.
motivation: Understanding how uniaxial heterostrain affects correlated phases in twisted bilayer graphene, which is a key material in condensed matter physics.
method: Self-consistent Hartree-Fock approach projected onto flat bands to compute band structure and interaction-induced gaps under varying strain.
result: Strain enhances bandwidth and suppresses insulating gaps, driving transitions to semimetallic states; effect depends on filling factor and strain direction.
conclusion: Uniaxial heterostrain is an effective tuning parameter for correlated phases in twisted bilayer graphene.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of the master stability function framework for analyzing synchronization stability in complex networks, covering pairwise, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) is a powerful tool, but a systematic investigation across various networked systems is lacking.
method: The paper formulates the MSF framework for pairwise coupled identical systems, extends it to directed and multilayer networks with intralayer and interlayer interactions, and analyzes higher-order networks. Numerical analysis and algorithms for computing MSF are provided.
result: A unified and simplified MSF analysis is presented for various network types, along with algorithms for stability regime identification and classification of MSF behaviors.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic study of MSF in coupled dynamical networks, making the tool more accessible, and highlights underexplored areas and emerging directions such as machine learning approaches for MSF estimation.

title: Classification And Correlation Signatures Of Chiral Spin Liquids On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Leon Balents And Yasir Iqbal Chunxiao Liu
abstract: We present a systematic classification and variational study of chiral quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice based on fermionic parton constructions. Focusing on chiral and spin-liquid Ansätze, we characterize their symmetry properties, flux structures, and low-energy spinon spectra within a projective symmetry group framework, and incorporate gauge fluctuations through Gutzwiller-projected wave functions studied by variational Monte Carlo. From the equal-time spin structure factor, we develop correlation-based diagnostics that distinguish gauge-dominated Coulomb phases from states with substantial matter-field and short-range contributions. Distinct chiral flux sectors, though close in energy, exhibit markedly different degrees of emergent gauge-field dominance, reflected in the geometry and contrast of pinch-point singularities. Although these states are not competitive ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model, they define a physically meaningful family of proximate chiral phases relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.
tldr: This paper classifies chiral spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice using parton constructions and variational Monte Carlo, focusing on symmetry and flux structures.
motivation: Chiral spin liquids are exotic quantum phases, but the paper's focus on pyrochlore lattice classification and correlation signatures does not align with the user's research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
method: The authors use fermionic parton constructions, projective symmetry group analysis, and Gutzwiller-projected wave functions with variational Monte Carlo to study chiral spin liquid Ansätze.
result: They identify distinct chiral flux sectors with different degrees of gauge-field dominance, reflected in pinch-point singularities in the spin structure factor.
conclusion: These chiral phases are not ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model but are relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.

title: Physical Sampling For Computational Photography
authors: Ni Chen And David J Brady
abstract: The standard model of photography is that lenses form images and focal planes capture those images. Over the past two decades, however, cameras have been transformed from devices that record focal images into analog-to-digital converters that transform massively parallel optical signals into serial electronic data. Under this new model, one may choose to maximize the quality and quantity of captured information, rather than focal image quality. Here we review the nature of the optical data stream and consider lens and focal plane designs that improve information capture capacity. After maximizing information capacity, the challenge of converting this information to digital data requires novel read-out and compression. We review strategies for approaching physical information limits under realistic size, power, and bandwidth constraints. Multiscale monocentric (spherical primary optics combined with arrays of secondary micro-cameras, each imaging a narrow subfield) and array lens architectures relax unfavorable geometric scaling by trading monolithic optics for co-designed system-level integration (jointly optimized optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems). Metaoptic and mode-sorting focal plane filters implement richer projection operators that sample spectral, polarimetric, and coherence features without requiring exhaustive scanning. Finally, because readout and computation dominate energy at high throughput, we highlight architectures that perform dimensionality reduction before (or during) digitization, including integrated photonic encoders and multilayer optical projections coupled to detection and learned decoding. Together, these developments motivate a shift from cameras optimized to produce 2D images toward cameras engineered as end-to-end information channels, co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout to deliver more task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
tldr: This paper reviews computational photography architectures that optimize information capture and compression under physical constraints, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to shift camera design from producing 2D images to end-to-end information channels, maximizing task-relevant measurements per photon and per joule.
method: The paper reviews multiscale monocentric optics, metaoptic filters, and integrated photonic encoders that perform dimensionality reduction before digitization.
result: It identifies architectures that improve information capacity and energy efficiency by co-designing optics, focal-plane, and readout subsystems.
conclusion: Future cameras should be engineered as information channels, leveraging co-design to overcome geometric scaling and readout bottlenecks.

title: Green’s Function Methods For Computing Supercurrents In Josephson Junctions
authors: Eduardo R Mucciolo, Jouko Nieminen, Xiao Xiao, Wei-Chi Chiu, Michael N Leuenberger And Arun Bansil
abstract: Interest in Josephson junctions (JJs) has increased rapidly in recent years not only because of their use in qubits and other quantum devices but also due to the unique physics supported by the JJs. The advent of various novel quantum materials for both the barrier region and the superconducting leads has led to the possibility of adding new functionalities to the JJs. Thus, there is a growing need for accurate modeling of the JJs and related systems to enable their predictive control and atomistic level understanding. This review presents an in-depth discussion of a Green’s-function-based formalism for computing supercurrents in JJs. The formulation is tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations and encompasses both dc and ac supercurrents. We hope that this review will provide a timely and comprehensive reference for researchers as well as beginning practitioners interested in Green’s-function-based methods to model supercurrents in JJs.
tldr: A review of Green's function methods for computing supercurrents in Josephson junctions, focusing on large-scale atomistic simulations.
motivation: Josephson junctions are key components in quantum devices, and accurate modeling is needed for predictive control and understanding of novel quantum materials.
method: The paper presents a Green's-function-based formalism tailored for large-scale atomistic simulations to compute both dc and ac supercurrents.
result: The formalism enables accurate modeling of supercurrents in Josephson junctions with various barrier and lead materials.
conclusion: This review provides a comprehensive reference for researchers using Green's function methods to model supercurrents in Josephson junctions.

title: Unlocking Complex Optical Vortices With Flat Optics
authors: Hammad Ahmed, Shumei Chen, Xibin Yang And Xianzhong Chen
abstract: Optical vortices (OVs) possess spiral wavefronts and quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM), allowing them to act as key carriers of information and enabling light to possess high-dimensional degrees of freedom. In the past decade, there has been a growing interest in investigating complex OVs. Nevertheless, conventional methods for generating such beams are limited by bulky setups, high costs, and restricted control. Optical metasurfaces have emerged as promising candidates to overcome these challenges in a compact and cost-effective platform with enhanced control. This review begins by presenting an advanced platform designed for manipulating OVs and then discusses emerging types of OVs, including composite, grafted, and comb-like structured light beams, as well as multispectral and arbitrarily shaped OVs, along with nonlinear metasurface approaches. Next, we review the recent progress in OAM detection and mode discrimination, highlighting current challenges for high-capacity OAM systems. After that, we emphasize key applications ranging from OAM-based holography for optical encryption to super-resolution microscopy, structured-light trapping, and quantum state engineering. Finally, we critically identify the key challenges and future prospects for metasurface-enabled OV technologies.
tldr: A review of metasurface-based generation and detection of complex optical vortices for high-dimensional information encoding.
motivation: Conventional methods for generating complex optical vortices are bulky and costly; metasurfaces offer a compact, cost-effective platform with enhanced control.
method: The paper reviews recent progress in metasurface designs for generating composite, grafted, comb-like, multispectral, and arbitrarily shaped optical vortices, as well as OAM detection and mode discrimination techniques.
result: Metasurface-enabled OV technologies enable applications in OAM-based holography, super-resolution microscopy, structured-light trapping, and quantum state engineering.
conclusion: Metasurface approaches hold promise for advancing OV-based information technologies, but challenges remain in scalability and integration.

title: Controlled Generation Of 3d Vortices In Driven Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Vijay Pal Singhludwig Matheyherwig Ottluigi Amicoahttps://ror.org/001kv2y39quantum Research Center, Technology Innovation Institute, Masdar City 9639, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emiratesbhttps://ror.org/00g30e956zentrum Für Optische Quantentechnologien And Institut Für Quantenphysik, Universität Hamburg, Hamburg 22761, Germanychttps://ror.org/0149pv473the Hamburg Centre For Ultrafast Imaging, Hamburg 22761, Germanydhttps://ror.org/01qrts582department Of Physics, Research Center OPTIMAS, Rheinland-Pfälzische Technische Universität Kaiserslautern-Landau, Kaiserslautern 67663, Germany

SignificanceUnderstanding how quantized vortices form, interact, and decay lies at the heart of quantum-fluid dynamics. We introduce a driven atomic Josephson junction as a versatile platform to create and control these excitations with single-cycle ...
tldr: This paper studies controlled generation of 3D vortices in driven atomic Josephson junctions, focusing on quantum fluid dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantized vortex formation and control is fundamental to quantum fluid dynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors introduce a driven atomic Josephson junction platform and demonstrate single-cycle vortex generation.
result: They achieve controlled creation and manipulation of 3D vortices in a Bose-Einstein condensate.
conclusion: The platform provides a versatile tool for studying vortex dynamics, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics.

title: Direct Measurement Of Out-of-Plane Thermal Conductivity Via Transient Depth Thermography
authors: Dmitrii Shymkiv, Chun Wang, Yan Jiang, Rajat Srivastava, Nandika D'souza, Yuzhe Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate measurement of out-of-plane thermal conductivity remains challenging, particularly for multilayer thin-film materials, due to the reliance of existing techniques on indirect, surface-sensitive observables. Here, we introduce transient depth thermography, a non-contact spectroscopic method that directly reconstructs spatiotemporal temperature profiles using time-resolved thermal radiation. By leveraging the wavelength-dependent optical penetration depth, the technique encodes depth information into the emission spectrum, enabling direct access to internal heat transport dynamics. We demonstrate the method on fused silica and MgF2, achieving agreement with established techniques while attaining an uncertainty of 2-5%. In addition, we measure the temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of MgF2 over a broad temperature range. Applicable to both bulk and thin-film systems, transient depth thermography provides a general and accurate framework for thermal characterization of complex materials.
tldr: This paper presents a non-contact optical method for measuring out-of-plane thermal conductivity in thin films using time-resolved thermal radiation.
motivation: Accurate measurement of out-of-plane thermal conductivity in multilayer thin films is challenging due to reliance on indirect surface-sensitive methods.
method: Transient depth thermography uses wavelength-dependent optical penetration depth to encode depth information into the emission spectrum, reconstructing spatiotemporal temperature profiles.
result: The method achieves 2-5% uncertainty on fused silica and MgF2, and measures temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of MgF2 over a broad range.
conclusion: Transient depth thermography provides a general and accurate framework for thermal characterization of complex bulk and thin-film materials.

title: Filter Shaping In Integrated Photonics Using Non-adiabatic Control
authors: Pierre Colman Abdullah Al-Abiad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that an array of integrated coupled waveguides can be designed to simultaneously perform the spectral filtering and routing of light. The framework that we present here operates in a regime opposite to the shortcut-to-adiabaticity techniques, but we show it nevertheless also only requires smooth, slow, and small, modulations of the array's parameters. Our design strategy rely on the analogy which exists between the temporal evolution of an Hamiltonian and the propagation of light in an array of coupled integrated waveguides, mimicking spatially in photonics phenomena analogue to the electronic transitions. Interestingly, the chromatic dispersion restores in photonics the correspondence between spatial propagation effect and wavelength dependence. Therefore our framework is able to fully reproduces temporal effects such as resonant transitions, making it suitable for filtering applications. As a design involving modulations, it shares similarities with Bragg-Gratings (BGs): but it adds some extra features that make it complementary in terms of applications and functionality. First it adds routing capability with the seamless management of multi-waveguide configuration. And secondly the framework we present requires only wavelength-scale modulations, order of magnitudes slower than for BGs. The effects we present here may not interfere with BGs geometry and functionality, and could even be combined with the latter.
tldr: This paper presents a method for spectral filtering and routing in integrated photonics using non-adiabatic control of coupled waveguides.
motivation: Integrated photonic devices require compact and efficient spectral filters and routers; existing approaches like Bragg gratings have limitations in modulation speed and routing capability.
method: The authors exploit the analogy between temporal Hamiltonian evolution and spatial light propagation in coupled waveguides, using smooth, slow modulations of waveguide parameters to achieve resonant transitions for filtering.
result: The proposed framework enables simultaneous spectral filtering and routing with wavelength-scale modulations, which are orders of magnitude slower than Bragg gratings, and can be combined with existing geometries.
conclusion: This approach offers a complementary method for integrated photonic filtering and routing, potentially improving device performance and integration density.

title: Greedy Fusion
authors: Andrew Schopieray
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that certain sequences of integer formal codegrees, motivated by the greedy algorithm for unit fraction decompositions of 1, dictate the structure of fusion rings. In particular, no fusion ring that has formal codegrees 2, 3, and 7 is categorifiable.
tldr: The paper studies fusion rings using greedy algorithm sequences of formal codegrees, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the structure and categorifiability of fusion rings via integer sequences.
method: Applies greedy algorithm for unit fraction decompositions to formal codegrees and analyzes fusion ring constraints.
result: Shows that no fusion ring with formal codegrees 2, 3, and 7 is categorifiable.
conclusion: The greedy algorithm provides a new tool for classifying fusion rings.

title: Overcoming Slow Kolmogorov Width Decay In Parametric Optimal Control Via Neural Network Surrogates
authors: Hendrik Kleikamp, Martin Lazar, Juan Ricardo Mu\~noz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we deal with parametric, linear-quadratic optimal control problems in which the solution can be uniquely characterized by the optimal final time adjoint state. As a motivating example, we establish theoretical results showing that for distributed control of the heat equation, the manifold of final time adjoints over the parameter space exhibits a slow decay of its Kolmogorov width if this was already the case for the parameter-dependent target states. Traditional linear reduced-order models would thus require a large reduced space in order to guarantee a sufficient accuracy, making them inefficient in this application. To overcome the limitation of linear models, we discuss a nonlinear surrogate based on U-Nets that maps parametric fields to approximate final time adjoints. We show that a suitable a posteriori error estimator remains applicable to the U-Net approximation and can be used to certify the surrogate results. Through two extensive numerical experiments, we show the potential of the U-Net surrogate and compare it with several linear and nonlinear methods from the literature. The results show that the U-Net consistently achieves the highest accuracy among the methods considered while requiring significantly fewer training samples.
tldr: This paper uses U-Net neural networks to overcome slow Kolmogorov width decay in parametric optimal control problems for the heat equation.
motivation: Traditional linear reduced-order models fail for parametric optimal control when the solution manifold has slow Kolmogorov width decay, making them inefficient.
method: The authors propose a U-Net-based nonlinear surrogate to map parametric fields to optimal final time adjoints, and show that an a posteriori error estimator can certify the approximation.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate that the U-Net surrogate achieves higher accuracy than linear and other nonlinear methods with fewer training samples.
conclusion: Neural network surrogates can effectively overcome the limitations of linear models in parametric optimal control, offering a certified and efficient alternative.

title: Construction Of Generalized Weighing-Hadamard Matrices Over Finite Fields
authors: Gustavo T. Bastos, Miguel Beltr\'a, Sara D. Cardell, Ver\'onica Requena
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence, several properties, and constructions of Generalized Weighing-Hadamard (GWH) matrices over finite fields are addressed in this work. We study the subset of invertible GWH matrices and show that it forms a group under matrix multiplication. Besides that, we introduce a strong notion of equivalence between such matrices, defined via orthogonal transformations, and further prove that the corresponding quotient group by the subgroup of orthogonal matrices is abelian. Finally, we discuss some applications of these matrices in coding theory.
tldr: This paper constructs and studies generalized weighing-Hadamard matrices over finite fields, focusing on their algebraic properties and applications in coding theory.
motivation: Generalized weighing-Hadamard matrices have applications in coding theory and signal processing, but their algebraic structure over finite fields is not fully understood.
method: The authors define invertible GWH matrices, show they form a group, introduce equivalence via orthogonal transformations, and prove the quotient group is abelian.
result: The set of invertible GWH matrices forms a group, and the quotient by orthogonal matrices is abelian; constructions and properties are provided.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of GWH matrices over finite fields, with potential applications in coding theory.

title: Norm-Cone Conjugation And Fenchel-Type Duality Beyond Convexity
authors: Miguel \'angel Melguizo-Padial Fernando Garc\'ia-Casta\~no
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a norm-cone conjugation scheme for extended-real-valued functions on normed spaces. The construction replaces affine minorants by translated norm-cones of the form \(x\mapsto r-\alpha\|x-x_0\|\), with \(\alpha\ge0\), and establishes a nonlinear conjugation framework underlying a Fenchel-type duality theory beyond convexity. The resulting conjugate is indexed by slopes and centres, and the associated biconjugate is the supremum of all norm-cone minorants lying below the function. We prove Fenchel--Young type inequalities, introduce admissible slopes and admissible heights, and characterize exact biconjugation in terms of norm-cone supportability. We also define a norm-cone subdifferential and relate it to exact support and biconjugation. Finally, we develop an abstract perturbation duality theory based on partial norm-cone conjugation in the perturbation variable. Weak duality holds without convexity assumptions, while strong duality follows from metric lower-bound conditions, including uniform lower Lipschitz estimates and lower calmness of the value function.
tldr: This paper introduces a norm-cone conjugation scheme for extended-real-valued functions on normed spaces, establishing a nonlinear conjugation framework and Fenchel-type duality beyond convexity.
motivation: To extend Fenchel duality to non-convex functions by replacing affine minorants with norm-cone minorants, enabling a broader class of optimization problems.
method: Defines a norm-cone conjugate indexed by slopes and centers, proves Fenchel-Young inequalities, introduces admissible slopes/heights, and develops a perturbation duality theory based on partial norm-cone conjugation.
result: Weak duality holds without convexity; strong duality follows from metric lower-bound conditions like uniform lower Lipschitz estimates.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to handle non-convex optimization via norm-cone supportability and subdifferentiability.

title: Energy Decay And Weak Observability For Some Evolution Systems
authors: Faouzi Triki Ka\"is Ammari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an abstract functional framework, we investigate the equivalence between two fundamental properties: weak observability and energy decay associated with certain classes of dissipative operators. This analysis is motivated by the study of evolution equations and their long-time behavior. Our main result establishes that under appropriate assumptions, these two notions are not only closely related but in fact equivalent. The proof relies on recent advances in the theory of weak observability, particularly those presented in , where new techniques have been developed to quantify the weak observability inequalities. These tools allow us to bridge the gap between qualitative decay properties and spectral estimates, offering a unified perspective on stability and control in abstract dynamical systems.
tldr: This paper proves the equivalence between weak observability and energy decay for dissipative evolution systems in an abstract functional framework.
motivation: Understanding the long-time behavior of evolution equations is important for stability and control theory.
method: The authors use recent advances in weak observability theory to establish inequalities that link observability to spectral estimates.
result: Under appropriate assumptions, weak observability and energy decay are shown to be equivalent.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on stability and control in abstract dynamical systems.

title: Characterization And Construction Of Pairwise Orthogonal Parseval Frames With Applications To Sampling
authors: Navneet Redhu, Anupam Gumber, Hartmut F\"uhr, Niraj K. Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide a characterization of pairwise orthogonal frames with generalized translation-invariant (GTI) structures, based on the unconditional convergence property (UCP). These GTI systems are generated by translating functions over a countable family of closed, co-compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian (LCA) group [MATH], where the families of subgroups associated with each system may differ. As an application of this characterization, we establish necessary and sufficient criteria for the orthogonality of various structured systems, including Gabor, wavelet, and shearlet systems on LCA groups. Furthermore, we derive a characterization of GTI Parseval (tight) frames and present explicit constructions of pairs of GTI systems using filters. Each constructed system satisfies the [MATH]-UCP and admits a Calder\'on sum equal to one. As a consequence of these results, the constructed systems form Parseval frames and are pairwise orthogonal. The proposed construction improves upon the technique in by relaxing the stationary assumption on the families of subgroups. Finally, we illustrate the results with examples using [MATH]-splines as generating functions and discuss applications of pairwise orthogonal frames in sampling theory.
tldr: This paper characterizes pairwise orthogonal Parseval frames with generalized translation-invariant structures on locally compact abelian groups, with applications to sampling theory.
motivation: To provide a unified characterization of pairwise orthogonal frames for various structured systems (Gabor, wavelet, shearlet) and to construct explicit examples with improved flexibility.
method: The authors use the unconditional convergence property (UCP) to characterize pairwise orthogonal GTI frames, and construct Parseval frames using filters with Calderón sum equal to one.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality of Gabor, wavelet, and shearlet systems are established, and explicit constructions of pairwise orthogonal Parseval frames are given.
conclusion: The results generalize previous constructions by relaxing stationary assumptions on subgroups, and have potential applications in sampling theory.

title: A Unified Framework For Reaction Systems Based On Interval Structures
authors: Paolo Bottoni, Anna Labella, Ion Petre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reaction systems have evolved into a rich family of computational models differing in their treatment of multiplicities, resource management, concurrency, and state evolution. We introduce a unified semantic framework based on interval structures and interval-based transformation systems. The framework decomposes operational semantics into independent resource, production, update, and execution strategies, providing a common basis for describing, comparing, and constructing reaction-system variants. We show that classical reaction systems, restricted reaction systems, multiset reaction systems, reaction systems with concentration, and resource-preserving multiset reaction systems are all recovered as instantiations of the framework. Quantitative reaction systems are accommodated through an additional preprocessing stage. We further demonstrate that the framework naturally extends beyond reaction systems to other computational models, including Petri nets. The proposed framework provides a common semantic foundation for existing models and a flexible basis for developing and analysing new computational formalisms.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified semantic framework for reaction systems based on interval structures, enabling comparison and construction of various computational models.
motivation: Reaction systems have diversified into many variants with different semantics, lacking a common foundation for analysis and comparison.
method: The authors introduce interval-based transformation systems that decompose operational semantics into independent strategies for resources, production, update, and execution.
result: Classical reaction systems, restricted reaction systems, multiset reaction systems, and others are recovered as instantiations; the framework also extends to Petri nets.
conclusion: The framework provides a flexible basis for developing and analyzing new computational formalisms beyond reaction systems.

title: Graph-Series Semantics And Abel Regularization For Recursive Hybrid Quantum Programs
authors: Jean-Pierre Magnot
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a graded graph-series semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs interpreted in the quantum orchestra monad. Finite terminating executions are represented by directed paths whose edges carry normal completely positive subunital maps and whose terminal vertices carry classical results. Path concatenation defines a graded execution category, while continuation grafting models outcome-dependent sequential composition. We construct a semantic evaluation from admissible execution-graph series to quantum orchestras and prove that it is compatible with both channel composition and Kleisli composition. For finitary recursive programs, the truncation of the execution series at degree [MATH] is shown to coincide with the [MATH]-th Kleene approximant of the associated Scott-continuous recursion functional. Consequently, evaluation of the complete graph series recovers the ordinary least-fixed-point denotation. Weighting a graph of degree [MATH] by [MATH], with [MATH], yields an Abel-regularised semantics whose Scott limit as [MATH] is the unregularised recursive denotation. Equivalently, the parametrisation [MATH] exponentially suppresses long executions and reconstructs the denotation as [MATH]. In a supplementary linear feedback sector, repeated recursion is represented by the execution resolvent [MATH]. We identify [MATH] with an algebraic cross-ratio of graph subspaces. Under Hilbert--Schmidt assumptions, the associated return operator is trace class and defines the Fredholm feedback determinant \( _{F}(I-qST), \) whose zeros detect singular feedback configurations and whose logarithmic expansion records closed loop traversals.
tldr: This paper introduces a graph-series semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs using Abel regularization, but it is highly abstract and mathematical with no clear connection to the user's research directions.
motivation: To provide a rigorous denotational semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs that can handle infinite executions via regularization.
method: The paper defines graded graph-series semantics in the quantum orchestra monad, uses path concatenation and continuation grafting, and applies Abel regularization to sum divergent series.
result: The truncation of execution series at degree n coincides with the n-th Kleene approximant, and the Abel-regularized semantics recovers the unregularized denotation in the limit.
conclusion: The framework provides a consistent semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs, but its practical relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics is unclear.

title: ReBound: Reuse-Aware Privacy For Interactive Decision Support
authors: Nada Lahjouji, Shufan Zhang, Xi He, Sharad Mehrotra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentially private decision support frameworks answer complex aggregate threshold queries with formal bounds on false negative and false positive rates, but treat each query independently with no memory of past results. In practice, analysts work interactively, issuing sequences of related queries that refine bounds, adjust thresholds, or derive new functions from previous ones. We propose ReBound, a framework that reuses cached results from previous queries to answer new queries at reduced or zero additional privacy cost while maintaining formal utility guarantees. ReBound introduces a reuse framework for multiple refinement types, a cache graph structure for efficient lookup of reusable results, and a negotiation mechanism for when requested bounds cannot be met within budget.
tldr: ReBound is a framework for reusing cached differentially private query results to reduce privacy cost in interactive decision support.
motivation: Existing differential privacy frameworks treat queries independently, ignoring that analysts often issue related queries interactively, leading to unnecessary privacy cost.
method: ReBound introduces a reuse framework for multiple refinement types, a cache graph for efficient lookup, and a negotiation mechanism for unmet bounds.
result: The framework enables answering new queries at reduced or zero additional privacy cost while maintaining formal utility guarantees.
conclusion: ReBound improves privacy efficiency in interactive settings by reusing past query results, but is focused on classical differential privacy, not quantum information.

title: Evaluating Encoding Strategies For Closed-Loop Classification In Biological Neural Networks
authors: Martin Schottlender, Veronika Volkova, Pengjie Zhou, Ruifeng Zheng, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Pit Hofmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacing with Biological Neural Networks (BNNs) requires encoding information into stimulation patterns that can be effectively processed and that enable the underlying system to adapt. Nevertheless, the role of stimulation encoding remains poorly understood. In this work, we compare multiple encoding strategies, including rate-based, phase-based, burst-based, and time-to-first-spike temporal encodings, in a closed-loop neural classification task using cultured BNNs. We encode visual inputs as spatiotemporal stimulation patterns delivered via a Multi-Electrode Array (MEA) and evaluate classification performance for each encoding scheme. We find that burst-based temporal encoding yields the highest observed performance, achieving up to 95.6 % accuracy in a binary classification task, compared to substantially lower performance from rate- and phase-based approaches. We further show that performance is highly sensitive to the spatial distribution of stimulation, with suboptimal electrode selection significantly degrading accuracy. These findings indicate that effective interfacing with biological neural systems requires the joint optimization of temporal and spatial encoding strategies, and highlight temporal encoding as a key design dimension for bio-digital computing.
tldr: This paper evaluates encoding strategies for closed-loop classification in biological neural networks, focusing on temporal and spatial stimulation patterns.
motivation: Effective interfacing with biological neural networks requires understanding how to encode information into stimulation patterns that the network can process and adapt to.
method: The authors compare rate-based, phase-based, burst-based, and time-to-first-spike temporal encodings in a closed-loop classification task using cultured BNNs on a multi-electrode array.
result: Burst-based temporal encoding achieves up to 95.6% accuracy in binary classification, outperforming rate- and phase-based approaches; performance is highly sensitive to spatial electrode selection.
conclusion: Effective bio-digital computing requires joint optimization of temporal and spatial encoding strategies, with temporal encoding being a key design dimension.

title: PriEval-Protect: A Unified Framework For Privacy Evaluation And Protection In Healthcare Systems
authors: Ilef Chebil, Asma El Hadj, Souheib Yousfi, Aroua Hedhili, Layth Sliman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safeguarding patient privacy while enabling meaningful healthcare data use remains critical under GDPR and HIPAA. Existing compliance methods are manual, error-prone, and separate policy audits from data-level assessments. This paper presents PriEval-Protect, a two-phase framework for unified privacy risk evaluation and mitigation. The evaluation phase combines regulatory compliance scoring using a fine-tuned legal LLM with RAG, and technical analysis via encryption type, data architecture, and metrics including similarity, uncertainty, adversary success, and information gain/loss. A composite risk score uses weighted aggregation via Analytic Hierarchy Process. The protection phase recommends countermeasures including federated learning and differential privacy based on assessed risk. Results on hospital documents and datasets demonstrate regulation-aligned, explainable assessments, bridging legal conformance and data-level risk analysis.
tldr: A framework for privacy evaluation and protection in healthcare systems using LLMs and risk metrics.
motivation: Existing compliance methods are manual and separate policy audits from data-level assessments, motivating a unified framework.
method: Combines regulatory compliance scoring via fine-tuned legal LLM with RAG and technical analysis using encryption type, data architecture, and metrics like similarity and adversary success, aggregated via AHP.
result: Demonstrates regulation-aligned, explainable assessments on hospital documents and datasets.
conclusion: The framework bridges legal conformance and data-level risk analysis for healthcare privacy.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
authors: Bartosz Prokop
Lendert Gelens
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression, network architectures, and decomposition techniques.
motivation: Biological systems are complex and often lack first-principles models; data-driven approaches can extract dynamics from time-resolved data.
method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques for discovering dynamical models from time-series data.
result: The review evaluates strengths, limitations, and complementarity of these approaches, providing a guide for selecting methods.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for biological modeling, but method choice depends on data characteristics and system complexity.

result: The model exhibits anomalous diffusion and non-Gaussian statistics, with distinct regimes in 1D and 2D.
conclusion: The pushy random walk provides a minimal framework for transport in deformable media, with potential applications in biophysics and materials science.

motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium carrier screening effects in ferroelectrics is important for energy-efficient electronics and memory applications.

result: The experiments demonstrate nonthermal suppression of ferroelectric order due to carrier screening on ultrafast timescales.

result: Effective diffusion coefficients depend on effective porosity and blocked domain width; spatial correlations can enhance or hinder diffusion depending on the arrangement.

motivation: Understanding mechanisms behind alternating stripes, clusters, and labyrinths observed in chemical reactions and biological systems like Min-protein dynamics and cardiac alternans.
method: The authors analyze a generic model of oscillatory media with spatially uniform and nonuniform global feedback, using theoretical and computational approaches.
result: They identify conditions and mechanisms leading to alternating pattern formation, showing how global feedback can induce period-2 spatiotemporal patterns.
conclusion: The work provides insights into pattern formation in oscillatory media, relevant to chemical and biological contexts, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine synchronization and swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators are important for understanding collective dynamics in active matter, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving reduced equations for the macroscopic order parameters and analyzing their stability and bifurcations.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for the onset of various collective states, including phase-locked, wave, and incoherent states, and validate them with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for studying swarmalator dynamics and can be extended to other coupled oscillator-swarm systems.

motivation: Granular materials exhibit reproducible volume fluctuations without thermal equilibration, and a quantitative statistical-mechanical description is needed.
