title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence to design metamaterials for wave manipulation using static diffusion fields.
motivation: To bridge the gap between static diffusion and dynamic wave propagation, enabling complex wave functionalities through simpler steady-state design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing wave parameters and fields to be obtained from static solutions.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, and experimentally validate a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints, merging static and dynamic physics.

title: Rashba-like Spin Splitting In Inversion Symmetric Plasmonic Metasurface
authors: Sujit Rajak, Nishkarsh Kumar, Dheeraj Yadav, Suman Mandal, Jeeban K Nayak, Ayan Banerjee, Subhasish Dutta Gupta, Olivier Martin And Nirmalya Ghosh
abstract: Spin-dependent dispersion and Rashba effect are manifestations of spin–orbit interaction (SOI) associated with the breaking of the spatial inversion symmetry in condensed matter and in optical systems. Here, we report an extraordinary spin-split dispersion effect of leaky surface plasmons in an inversion-symmetric plasmonic crystal. Momentum domain polarization analysis identified a transverse momentum-dependent linear birefringence–linear dichroism (geometric LB–LD) effect responsible for this phenomena. It is demonstrated that evolution of strong geometrical phase gradient due to the geometric LB–LD effect mediates the spin-split dispersion in inversion symmetric plasmonic metasurface through spin (circular polarization)-dependent transverse momentum. This unconventional SOI phenomena offers a new paradigm of spin-based dispersion engineering and spin-controlled nano-optical functionalities by encompassing the forbidden class of symmetric metastructures in the realm of spin optics.
tldr: This paper reports a spin-split dispersion effect in an inversion-symmetric plasmonic metasurface due to geometric phase gradients, demonstrating a new spin-orbit interaction phenomenon.
motivation: To explore spin-dependent dispersion and Rashba-like effects in optical systems without spatial inversion symmetry breaking, enabling new spin-controlled nano-optical functionalities.
method: Momentum domain polarization analysis is used to identify a transverse momentum-dependent linear birefringence–linear dichroism (geometric LB–LD) effect, which mediates the spin-split dispersion.
result: A strong geometrical phase gradient due to the geometric LB–LD effect leads to spin-dependent transverse momentum and spin-split dispersion in an inversion-symmetric plasmonic metasurface.
conclusion: This unconventional spin-orbit interaction offers a new paradigm for spin-based dispersion engineering and spin-controlled nano-optics using symmetric metastructures.

title: Half Dualization And Non-invertible Particle-vortex Duality Defect On Lattice
authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce half dualization as a general principle to construct non-invertible duality defects. The construction performs a duality transformation only in a subregion of spacetime, leaving an interface between the original theory and its dual. A non-invertible duality defect can be hosted on this interface. Half dualization is applicable whenever a local duality transformation is available, and does not depend on the spacetime dimension. We demonstrate the construction procedure in the (2+1)-dimensional Villainized charge-[MATH] XY model on a cubic lattice. Half dualization yields a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect whose fusion with its orientation reverse produces a (1+1)-dimensional [MATH] gauge theory on the fusion surface. We then apply half dualization to the [MATH]-gauged XY model relevant to the 3D XY[MATH] transition. In the gauged model, the half dualization interface hosts a gauge covariant duality wall, rather than a genuine gauge invariant duality defect. It flows to an invertible duality defect in infrared when the [MATH] gauge theory is confined or Higgsed.
tldr: This paper introduces half dualization to construct non-invertible particle-vortex duality defects in lattice models, focusing on the (2+1)-dimensional XY model.
motivation: To develop a general principle for constructing non-invertible duality defects that can be applied to various theories and dimensions.
method: Half dualization is performed on a subregion of spacetime, creating an interface between the original theory and its dual, which hosts the duality defect. The construction is demonstrated on the Villainized XY model on a cubic lattice.
result: The half dualization yields a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect whose fusion with its orientation reverse produces a (1+1)-dimensional gauge theory on the fusion surface. In the gauged XY model, the interface hosts a gauge covariant duality wall that flows to an invertible duality defect in the infrared.
conclusion: Half dualization provides a systematic way to construct non-invertible duality defects, with potential applications in studying dualities and phase transitions in lattice field theories.

title: Reconstruct The Ambient Noise Source From The Multi-frequency Sparse Correlation Data

abstract: ArXiv:2607.13509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel multi-frequency factorization method to reconstruct the spatial support of the ambient noise source. The proposed method only requires sparse correlation data and has low computational cost. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops a multi-frequency factorization method to reconstruct the spatial support of ambient noise sources from sparse correlation data.
motivation: Reconstructing ambient noise sources is important for applications like seismic imaging and ocean acoustics, but existing methods require dense data or high computational cost.
method: The authors propose a novel multi-frequency factorization method that uses sparse correlation data and has low computational cost, with numerical experiments in 2D and 3D.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in reconstructing the spatial support of ambient noise sources.
conclusion: The method provides an efficient way to reconstruct noise sources from sparse data, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Impacts Of Social And Impact Heterogeneity On Social-climate Outcomes
authors: Amrita Punnavajhala, Brian Beckage, Madhur Anand, Daniele Visioni, Jared Farley, Chris T. Bauch
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regional heterogeneity in social characteristics, temperature change, and vulnerability to climate impacts is likely to influence the magnitude of anthropogenic climate change, but has not been considered in coupled social-climate models, which seek to represent interactions between social and climate dynamics. Here, we examine how the projected mean global temperature anomaly and population support for mitigation respond to heterogeneity in these factors across five regions of the world, using a coupled social-climate model. We find that heterogeneity in climate impacts increases the temperature anomaly by 0.2[MATH]C, while social heterogeneity increases it by an additional 0.1[MATH]C. The projected temperature anomaly also increases with higher variability in climate impacts across regions, even for the same average global climate impact. Finally, we identify a social-climate tipping point, where low vulnerability to impacts under existing social conditions in one region can tip the system into an alternative slow-mitigation, high-temperature state. Our results show that heterogeneity in climate impacts leads to higher global mean temperatures and efforts to reduce global disparities could improve both social and climate outcomes.
tldr: This paper studies how regional heterogeneity in social characteristics and climate impacts affects global temperature and mitigation support using a coupled social-climate model.
motivation: Regional heterogeneity in social factors and climate impacts is likely to influence climate change outcomes but has not been considered in coupled social-climate models.
method: The authors develop a coupled social-climate model with five world regions and simulate the effects of heterogeneity in social characteristics, temperature change, and vulnerability to climate impacts.
result: Heterogeneity in climate impacts increases the temperature anomaly by 0.2°C, social heterogeneity adds another 0.1°C, and a social-climate tipping point is identified where low vulnerability in one region leads to a high-temperature state.
conclusion: Reducing global disparities could improve both social and climate outcomes, as heterogeneity leads to higher global mean temperatures.

title: Overlapping Window Tests For Correlation And Trend
authors: Abbas Alhakim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general framework for constructing and analyzing overlapping sliding-window statistics for dependence and trend detection. For a fixed window size, the overlapping blocks form a Markov chain, and the asymptotic variance of any centered window statistic is determined by the covariance operator of this chain. Using its spectral structure, we obtain an orthogonal decomposition of the space of window functions into components associated with different overlap levels. This leads to a natural notion of incremental dependence information: the part of a statistic that captures exactly the new information introduced by enlarging the window. We give an explicit procedure for extracting these components and apply the method to two classes of examples. For correlation detection, we study symmetric polynomial window functions and identify their informative projected part. For trend detection, we analyze localized rank-based statistics and isolate the contribution of the largest newly introduced lag. The examples also show that different statistics may exhibit different local detection scales, including nonclassical ones. The same viewpoint leads to a natural quantitative measure of incremental information, which can be used to assess how much new dependence structure is captured as the window size increases, and to guide scale selection. Overall, the paper provides a systematic method for designing overlapping-window tests and deriving their asymptotic normalization and local behavior.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for overlapping sliding-window statistics for dependence and trend detection, with applications to correlation and trend detection.
motivation: To provide a systematic method for designing overlapping-window tests and understanding the incremental dependence information as window size increases.
method: The authors model overlapping blocks as a Markov chain, use spectral decomposition to orthogonalize window functions, and extract components capturing new information at each overlap level.
result: They obtain an orthogonal decomposition of window functions, identify informative components for symmetric polynomial and rank-based statistics, and propose a quantitative measure of incremental information.
conclusion: The framework offers a principled way to design and normalize overlapping-window tests, with potential for scale selection in dependence detection.

title: A Generative Model-Free Form Deformation Approach For The Generation Of Mesh Motions With Applications To Pde
authors: Gugliemo Padula, Artem Sinitsa, Gianluigi Rozza
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a topology-agnostic framework for matching deformations of three-dimensional shapes with non-isomorphic mesh graphs by modelling the deformation as the flow of an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE). The velocity field is parameterised by a time-dependent Free Form Deformation (FFD), expressed through displacements of a coarse control lattice, yielding a smooth and low-dimensional representation that decouples the deformation model from the discretisation of the source and target surfaces. Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the induced ODE map is a universal approximator (in the sup norm) for mappings between genus-0 surfaces, providing a theoretical expressivity guarantee. To further compress the representation and enable probabilistic inference, we couple the ODE--FFD model with a flow-based generative approach in the TarFlow framework, learning a compact latent parametrisation over time series of FFD maps. The resulting method supports efficient sampling and optimisation of plausible deformation trajectories while preserving mesh quality, and it enables scalable reduced-order modelling. Experiments on deforming-body flow benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency of reduced-order models constructed from the learned latent dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a generative model-free form deformation approach for mesh motions with applications to PDEs.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a topology-agnostic framework for matching deformations of 3D shapes with non-isomorphic mesh graphs, enabling efficient reduced-order modeling for deforming-body flow problems.
method: They model deformation as an ODE flow, parameterize the velocity field using time-dependent Free Form Deformation (FFD), and couple it with a flow-based generative model (TarFlow) to learn a compact latent parametrization.
result: The method provides a universal approximation guarantee for genus-0 surface mappings and demonstrates improved accuracy and computational efficiency in reduced-order models on deforming-body flow benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a scalable and efficient approach for generating mesh motions and reduced-order models, with potential applications in computational fluid dynamics and shape analysis.

title: A Unified Approach For Testing In Hilbert Spaces On Incomplete Data
authors: Philipp W\"ubbolding Daniel Gaigall
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider statistical testing on the basis of incomplete observations with values in a separable Hilbert space, where the dimension is possibly large or even infinite. The general Hilbert space setting allows various data types as they arise in modern applications, in particular high dimensional and functional data. Possible Hilbert space testing problems are goodness-of-fit, symmetry, homogeneity and independence. We present an approach for modeling incomplete data that covers several problems in practice, e.g., ultra high dimensional random vectors with missing entries or partially observed stochastic processes. We identify a specific structure (independent and identically distributed) in the incomplete data that enables the analysis of statistical procedures with the help of suitable mathematical results (e.g., laws of large numbers and central limit theorems). Additionally, a general and novel concept for testing different hypotheses in this situation is suggested and sketched for the example of testing goodness-of-fit for normality.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified statistical testing framework for incomplete data in Hilbert spaces, covering high-dimensional and functional data.
motivation: Incomplete data (e.g., missing entries, partially observed processes) is common in modern applications, but existing testing methods are often ad-hoc or limited to specific settings.
method: The authors model incomplete data as independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations in a separable Hilbert space, and develop a general concept for testing hypotheses such as goodness-of-fit, symmetry, homogeneity, and independence.
result: The approach leverages laws of large numbers and central limit theorems in Hilbert spaces to enable analysis of statistical procedures, and is illustrated for testing normality.
conclusion: The paper provides a unified theoretical framework for hypothesis testing with incomplete functional or high-dimensional data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Almost Disjoint Families And Johnson-Lindenstrauss Spaces
authors: Antonio Avil\'es, Grzegorz Plebanek, Luis S\'aenz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every almost disjoint family [MATH] of infinite subsets of [MATH] gives rise to a scattered compact space [MATH] and a family of Johnson-Lindenstrauss spaces JL[MATH]. We consider almost disjoint families arising from finitely branching trees and investigate whether they define homeomorphic compacta and isomorphic Banach spaces.
tldr: This paper studies almost disjoint families of subsets of natural numbers and their associated Johnson-Lindenstrauss Banach spaces, focusing on topological and isomorphic properties.
motivation: To understand the structure of scattered compact spaces and Banach spaces arising from almost disjoint families defined by finitely branching trees.
method: The authors consider almost disjoint families constructed from finitely branching trees and analyze the homeomorphism type of the associated compact spaces and isomorphism type of the Banach spaces.
result: They investigate conditions under which different trees yield homeomorphic compacta or isomorphic Banach spaces.
conclusion: The work contributes to set-theoretic topology and Banach space theory, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Model Predictive Control For Laser Thermal Processing: Operator Learning, Closed-loop Validation, And Out-of-distribution Analysis
authors: Smajil Halilovic, Yuchen Zhang, Daniel M. Tartakovsky
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laser-based thermal processing, such as laser powder bed fusion, requires tight regulation of the peak surface temperature: heat accumulates where the moving source re-enters previously heated material, driving the temperature out of its process window and causing defects. High-fidelity thermal models capture this physics but are too slow for online optimization, which motivates fast, differentiable, and generalizable surrogates. We develop and validate a complete surrogate-based control pipeline that regulates the maximum surface temperature of a moving laser on a 304-stainless-steel substrate. We also determine conditions under which our surrogate can be trusted inside the control loop by probing its out-of-distribution limits. A key component of our surrogate is a multi-step deep operator network bespoke for moving sources: its branch subnetwork encodes the future power and trajectory (position and velocity) sequence, while its trunk encodes the current peak temperature and the temperature at the future laser locations, yielding a one-shot five-step prediction. By way of illustration, we use this surrogate as a smooth (algebraic-rectifier) nonlinear program inside a receding-horizon model predictive controller solved in CasADi/IPOPT. The surrogate forward pass is over thousand times faster than the equivalent finite-difference steps. We show that aggregate open-loop accuracy is necessary but not sufficient for control-readiness: two surrogates with near-identical offline error behave drastically differently in closed loop. A controlled two-ensemble data design reduces a 91 K path-corner underprediction failure to 1.4 K, and a calibrated one-sided constraint margin of 13 K yields zero violations of the true upper bound on all tested paths.
tldr: This paper develops a surrogate-based model predictive control pipeline for laser thermal processing, focusing on operator learning and closed-loop validation.
motivation: Laser-based thermal processing requires tight temperature regulation to avoid defects, but high-fidelity models are too slow for online optimization.
method: A multi-step deep operator network is used as a surrogate to predict temperature, integrated into a receding-horizon model predictive controller solved with CasADi/IPOPT.
result: The surrogate is over 1000 times faster than finite-difference steps; a two-ensemble data design reduces prediction failure from 91 K to 1.4 K, and a calibrated margin yields zero violations.
conclusion: Aggregate open-loop accuracy is necessary but not sufficient for control-readiness; the surrogate-based control pipeline is effective for laser thermal processing.

title: Hybrid Gkb Methods For X-Ray Tomography Problems With Unmatched Back Projector
authors: Rosemary Renaut Abdulmajeed Alsubhi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: X ray Computed Tomography (CT) is a widely used imaging modality in medical, industrial, and scientific applications. In practical CT implementations, forward, A, and back projection, B, operators are often constructed using different discretization schemes to improve computational efficiency on available software and hardware platforms. Consequently, the resulting projector pair is generally unmatched, meaning that the back projector is not the exact adjoint of the forward projector. This mismatch alters the mathematical properties of the reconstruction problem and can affect the convergence behavior of iterative reconstruction methods. Previous studies have proposed AB and BA Golub Kahan bidiagonalization (GKB) methods, as well as GMRES and hybrid GMRES methods, for solving CT reconstruction problems with unmatched projector pairs, demonstrating reduced semiconvergence effects compared with conventional approaches. In this work, we develop hybrid variants of the AB- and BA-GKB algorithms by incorporating regularization within the projection process. The singular value decomposition for the operator on the projected space is used to efficiently reconstruct the solution, and to automatically select the regularization parameter using either the L-curve or generalized cross-validation. Numerical experiments on several CT reconstruction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid methods in improving robustness against semiconvergence.
tldr: This paper develops hybrid GKB methods for CT reconstruction with unmatched forward/back projector pairs, focusing on computational efficiency and regularization.
motivation: In practical CT, forward and back projectors are often mismatched due to different discretization schemes, which degrades convergence of iterative methods. Existing GKB methods reduce semiconvergence but lack regularization.
method: Hybrid variants of AB- and BA-GKB algorithms are proposed, incorporating regularization via SVD on the projected space and automatic parameter selection using L-curve or GCV.
result: Numerical experiments on CT reconstruction problems show improved robustness against semiconvergence compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: The hybrid GKB methods effectively handle unmatched projector pairs and enhance reconstruction quality in CT imaging.

title: Residual-Christoffel Sampling For Random Feature Collocation Of Linear PDEs
authors: Yangshuai Wang Jiale Linghu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random feature collocation fixes a randomly generated trial space and determines its coefficients from a linear least-squares system. Stability then depends on whether the sampled residual equations represent the geometry induced by the differential operator. We construct an operator-aware discretization in which the operator-applied features determine both the collocation measure and a coefficient whitening map. The randomized scheme combines a residual-Christoffel density with inverse-density weights, while a deterministic scalar-row alternative maximizes successive regularized log-determinant increments. Conditional on the realized trial space, the sampled whitened interior Gram is a spectral approximation to the reference Gram on the retained residual space, with sample complexity linear in the retained dimension up to a logarithmic factor. For uniformly analytic residual kernels, the associated operator has stretched-exponentially decaying eigenvalues and ridge effective dimension that is polylogarithmic in the inverse ridge scale. Experiments on scalar and vector equations, varied geometries, and one to three spatial dimensions show that residual-space sampling and whitening produce numerically full-rank transformed systems with substantially smaller condition numbers and iteration counts. The deterministic construction attains the lowest errors at the smallest scalar sample sizes. Residual-space geometry therefore yields a principled design for stable strong-form random feature collocation.
tldr: This paper proposes a residual-Christoffel sampling method for random feature collocation of linear PDEs, focusing on numerical stability and efficiency.
motivation: Random feature collocation methods suffer from ill-conditioned systems; the authors aim to design an operator-aware discretization that improves stability and sample complexity.
method: They construct a residual-Christoffel density combined with inverse-density weights and a deterministic scalar-row alternative that maximizes regularized log-determinant increments, then analyze the spectral approximation properties of the whitened Gram matrix.
result: The method achieves numerically full-rank transformed systems with lower condition numbers and iteration counts; sample complexity is linear in retained dimension up to a logarithmic factor.
conclusion: Residual-space geometry provides a principled design for stable strong-form random feature collocation, demonstrated on various PDEs.

title: Computing Strong Rank-Revealing Factorizations For Matrices With Orthonormal Rows
authors: Anil Damle
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a pivoting strategy due to Stewart (based on work by Bischof) computes a strong rank-revealing factorization when applied to a matrix with orthonormal rows. When paired with the classical column selection algorithm of Golub, Klema, and Stewart (GKS) it helps achieve rank-[MATH] approximation accuracy bounds and basis conditioning as good as those from applying a strong rank-revealing factorization directly to A. We then extend this framework in two directions: (1) providing analysis of GKS when only approximations of right singular vectors are available and (2) providing a randomized variant of the pivoting strategy for matrices with orthonormal rows that achieves the same theoretical guarantees but can return the desired subset two orders of magnitude faster than the deterministic variant.
tldr: This paper presents algorithms for computing strong rank-revealing factorizations of matrices with orthonormal rows, with applications in numerical linear algebra.
motivation: Strong rank-revealing factorizations are important for low-rank approximations and subset selection, but existing algorithms may not be efficient for matrices with orthonormal rows.
method: The paper analyzes Stewart's pivoting strategy for matrices with orthonormal rows, extends the GKS algorithm to handle approximate singular vectors, and introduces a randomized variant for faster computation.
result: The proposed methods achieve approximation accuracy and basis conditioning comparable to direct strong rank-revealing factorizations, with the randomized variant being up to two orders of magnitude faster.
conclusion: The algorithms provide efficient and accurate tools for rank-revealing factorizations in numerical linear algebra, but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Spectrally Damped Tensor Randomized Kaczmarz Method For Doubly Noisy Tensor Systems
authors: Jiyoung Choi Nahyun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor randomized Kaczmarz (TRK) methods are efficient row-action solvers for tensor linear systems under the t-product framework. We study their behavior under a doubly noisy perturbation model. In this model, both the system tensor and the right-hand side tensor are corrupted. We first analyze standard TRK and derive an expected error recursion with two terms. One term is contractive, and the other is a persistent perturbation term. This explains the noise-limited and semi-convergent behavior that can occur when the observed tensor system is inconsistent. We then introduce a spectrally damped tensor randomized Kaczmarz method (SD-TRK). We prove an expected error recursion for SD-TRK that separates error propagation from noise injection. The bound makes explicit a speed-robustness trade-off. We also give an FFT-based implementation that applies the damped update slice-wise in the Fourier domain. This implementation allows frequency-dependent damping parameters in practice. Numerical experiments on synthetic tensor systems illustrate the stabilization behavior of SD-TRK relative to standard TRK in noisy and ill-conditioned settings. We also include a two-pass image reconstruction comparison under the same noisy reconstruction pipeline.
tldr: This paper proposes a spectrally damped tensor randomized Kaczmarz method for solving tensor linear systems with noise in both the system tensor and right-hand side.
motivation: Standard tensor randomized Kaczmarz methods exhibit noise-limited and semi-convergent behavior when the observed tensor system is inconsistent due to double-sided noise.
method: The authors introduce a spectrally damped variant (SD-TRK) that uses frequency-dependent damping parameters in the Fourier domain via an FFT-based implementation, and derive expected error recursions.
result: The SD-TRK method separates error propagation from noise injection, providing a speed-robustness trade-off, and numerical experiments show stabilization in noisy and ill-conditioned settings.
conclusion: The proposed method improves robustness to noise in tensor linear systems, with potential applications in image reconstruction.

title: Spectral-Informed Neural Networks Outperform Spectral Methods In High-dimensional PDEs
authors: Ivan Oseledets Tianchi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For low-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods can achieve exceptionally high accuracy. For middle-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods remain feasible through specific techniques such as sparse grids or hyperbolic cross. However, for high-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods suffer frome the curse of dimensionality. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising approach to overcome this challenge, offering scalability to high dimensions, but often suffer from limited accuracy and efficiency. Recently proposed spectral-informed neural networks (SINNs) combine spectral methods with PINNs, operating directly in the spectral domain to avoid spatial derivative computations and to reduce memory consumption. In this work, we introduce Modified SINNs, which integrate coefficient decay scaling and basis embeddings motivated by harmonic analysis to enhance accuracy in high-dimensional problems and enable accurate approximation of unknown spectral coefficients. Numerical experiments on steady and time-dependent partial differential equations demonstrate that Modified SINNs outperform sparse grid spectral methods on middle-dimensional problems with incomplete spectral information and achieve superior accuracy compared to PINNs on high-dimensional problems.
tldr: This paper proposes Modified Spectral-Informed Neural Networks (SINNs) for solving high-dimensional PDEs, combining spectral methods with physics-informed neural networks.
motivation: Spectral methods suffer from the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional problems, while PINNs offer scalability but limited accuracy. The authors aim to combine the strengths of both approaches.
method: Modified SINNs integrate coefficient decay scaling and basis embeddings motivated by harmonic analysis, operating directly in the spectral domain to avoid spatial derivative computations.
result: Numerical experiments show that Modified SINNs outperform sparse grid spectral methods on middle-dimensional problems with incomplete spectral information and achieve superior accuracy compared to PINNs on high-dimensional problems.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively enhances accuracy and efficiency for high-dimensional PDEs, demonstrating the potential of spectral-informed neural networks.

title: Approximation Of Solutions Of Parameter-dependent Problems By Residual Neural Networks
authors: Ana Carpio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a convergent scheme to train neural networks involving analytic activation functions based on gradient flows. Convergence properties are guaranteed by Lojasiewicz theory. The main advantage of this approach is its simplicity of implementation. The coefficients of the network are approximated by solving a system of ordinary differential equations. We test the method by constructing residual neural network approximations of solutions of parametric problems. The dependence of the solutions of simple ordinary differential equations on a few parameters is correctly reproduced. The solutions of inverse problems involving wave constraints which depend on a few parameters can be reasonably approximated, even in regions in which the problem is severely ill posed.
tldr: This paper develops a convergent training scheme for residual neural networks to approximate solutions of parameter-dependent problems, using gradient flows and Lojasiewicz theory.
motivation: To provide a simple and theoretically grounded method for training neural networks to solve parametric problems, including inverse problems with wave constraints.
method: The network coefficients are approximated by solving a system of ordinary differential equations derived from gradient flows, with convergence guaranteed by Lojasiewicz theory.
result: The method correctly reproduces solutions of simple ODEs depending on a few parameters and reasonably approximates solutions of inverse problems with wave constraints, even in severely ill-posed regions.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a simple implementation with guaranteed convergence, suitable for parametric problems and inverse problems.

title: The Value Of Perfect Endpoint Forecasts For Offshore-Wind Thermal Firming
authors: Arash Khojaste, Geoffrey Pritchard, Golbon Zakeri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecast value depends not only on accuracy but also on the information structure available to the operating model. We study a diagnostic current-endpoint-only forecast for offshore-wind thermal firming: at hour t, the controller observes the current net-demand state z_t and one perfect future target z_{t+h}, but not the intermediate path or earlier endpoint messages. Unlike rolling path forecasts, these endpoint information sets are not nested in h. We embed the signal in a cyclostationary MDP using quantile Fourier regression states estimated from ISO New England load and offshore wind data, and solve annual state-action-frequency LPs for h = 1, . . . , 6. A one-hour endpoint forecast reduces annual firming cost by 8.07%, while a six-hour endpoint reduces it by 2.28%. The decreasing profile shows that a single farther endpoint is less actionable for a one-step ramping decision, without implying that longer rolling forecasts are less valuable.
tldr: This paper studies the value of perfect endpoint forecasts for offshore-wind thermal firming using a cyclostationary MDP.
motivation: To understand how forecast information structure affects operational cost reduction in renewable energy integration.
method: Embed a current-endpoint-only forecast in a cyclostationary MDP with quantile Fourier regression states, solving annual state-action-frequency LPs for different forecast horizons.
result: A one-hour endpoint forecast reduces annual firming cost by 8.07%, while a six-hour endpoint reduces it by 2.28%.
conclusion: A single farther endpoint is less actionable for one-step ramping decisions, but this does not imply longer rolling forecasts are less valuable.

title: Operational Evidence Gaps For LLMs In Fraud Detection And Trust-and-Safety Workflows
authors: Keyur Gabani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are now proposed for fraud detection, scam investigation, content moderation, and other trust-and-safety workflows. Much of the public literature still evaluates them as models, with less attention to their behavior as components in operational pipelines. This creates a practical evidence question: what would justify placing an LLM inside a live workflow with latency, cost, escalation, human-review, and adversarial-risk constraints? We address this question through a fraud-first survey of deployment evidence. We code 49 operationally relevant sources on LLM use in fraud detection, investigation support, content moderation, and cross-cutting robustness (18 fraud, 14 moderation, 17 cross-cutting), supplemented by 15 contextual references that establish the survey boundaries. These sources include systems, benchmarks, frameworks, and deployment-relevant surveys, not 49 production deployments. The main finding is an evidence imbalance. Fraud supplies the largest task-specific portion of the coded corpus. The moderation papers, however, include more explicit public evidence on latency, cost, governance, and fairness. Among the 18 fraud and investigation sources, none report clean per-decision latency, per-decision dollar cost, or calibration evidence; most report offline task performance, retrieval gains, or case-study accuracy instead. The survey contributes a role-and-evidence organizing frame, FORTE, for locating LLMs as classifiers, retrieval interfaces, explanation generators, reviewer assistants, agents, feature extractors, or escalation components. It also contributes a minimum deployment-evidence checklist covering latency budget, cost per decision, decision threshold, explanation integrity, and adversarial pressure. The resulting agenda identifies studies needed to support deployment claims for LLM-based fraud and trust-and-safety work.
tldr: This paper surveys operational evidence gaps for deploying LLMs in fraud detection and trust-and-safety workflows, finding a lack of latency, cost, and calibration data.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly proposed for fraud detection and content moderation, but public evaluations focus on model performance rather than operational pipeline constraints like latency, cost, and adversarial risk.
method: The authors conduct a fraud-first survey of 49 operationally relevant sources, coding them by role and evidence type, and propose the FORTE organizing frame and a minimum deployment-evidence checklist.
result: Fraud detection sources lack per-decision latency, cost, and calibration evidence; moderation papers include more explicit public evidence on these operational metrics.
conclusion: There is a significant evidence gap for deploying LLMs in live fraud and trust-and-safety workflows, and the paper provides an agenda for future studies to fill these gaps.

title: SingGuard-NSFA: Extensible Guardrails For Agentic Ai Via Generative Reasoning And Real-Time Classification
authors: Singguard Team
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present nsfaguard, a guardrail framework for securing agentic AI systems against operational threats, such as prompt injection, sensitive information extraction, malicious code requests, dangerous tool misuse, and resource exhaustion. We first introduce the NSFA taxonomy, which organizes 185 risk variants into a CIA-triad-grounded hierarchy and is cross-validated against three well-established OWASP guidelines. Based on this taxonomy, we construct a benchmark suite spanning 133 languages, comprising over 93K purpose-built samples targeting both user queries and agent responses, along with 3,435 cross-source samples adapted from five public agent-security datasets. To detect these operational threats in practice, we develop a dual-mode approach combining SFT-based generative reasoning for interpretable offline auditing with discriminative classification heads on the frozen backbone, enabling real-time detection at approximately 50,ms. We release four models with 0.8B, 2B, 4B, and 9B parameters, all achieving [MATH]94% F1 on purpose-built benchmarks and surpassing the strongest competing guardrails by 6 to 12 absolute points. On cross-source evaluation, the 9B model attains 91.29% F1 with a more balanced precision--recall trade-off. Moreover, ablation experiments show that classification heads can equip a guardrail with risk detection capabilities beyond its original scope and achieve state-of-the-art performance. These results demonstrate the extensibility of the approach and its generality as a plug-in enhancement.
tldr: A guardrail framework for securing agentic AI systems against operational threats using a dual-mode approach combining generative reasoning and real-time classification.
motivation: Agentic AI systems face operational threats like prompt injection and tool misuse, requiring robust guardrails.
method: Introduces NSFA taxonomy with 185 risk variants, builds a benchmark of 93K samples, and develops a dual-mode approach with SFT-based generative reasoning for offline auditing and discriminative classification heads for real-time detection.
result: Models achieve >94% F1 on purpose-built benchmarks, surpassing competitors by 6-12 points; 9B model attains 91.29% F1 on cross-source evaluation.
conclusion: The approach is extensible and achieves state-of-the-art performance as a plug-in enhancement for agentic AI security.

title: Beyond AI-Generated Labels: Watermarking, Co-Creation, And Conflation Of AI-Generation With Disinformation
authors: Giovanni Spitale Federico Germani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Watermarking is often presented as a straightforward solution for distinguishing AI-generated from human-generated content, enabling platforms and regulators to trace synthetic content and detect AI-generated outputs at scale. This paper examines whether such mechanisms meaningfully address the epistemic and ethical challenges that arise in domains where the central concern is not the automation of content production, but the accuracy, intent, and deceptive potential of messages. We argue that extending watermark-based approaches to these settings is conceptually and practically misguided. Invisible watermarking encodes only model origin; when operationalized into visible AI-generated labels, it reduces complex creative processes to a misleading binary and provides no information about truthfulness. Such labels may stigmatize legitimate uses of generative tools while encouraging misplaced trust in unmarked content. Here we propose an alternative approach centered on process transparency and information literacy. We argue that these measures address the epistemic and ethical dimensions of AI-generated disinformation more effectively than visible watermark labels, reframing authorship as a transparent human practice rather than a binary indicator of machine involvement.
tldr: This paper critiques watermarking as a solution for AI-generated content, arguing it conflates AI-generation with disinformation and proposing process transparency instead.
motivation: The authors aim to address the epistemic and ethical challenges of distinguishing AI-generated from human-generated content, particularly in contexts where accuracy and intent are central.
method: The paper provides a conceptual analysis of watermarking and AI-generation labels, examining their limitations and proposing an alternative framework based on process transparency and information literacy.
result: The authors conclude that visible AI-generation labels are misleading and may stigmatize legitimate uses while encouraging misplaced trust in unmarked content.
conclusion: Process transparency and information literacy are more effective than watermarking for addressing the epistemic and ethical dimensions of AI-generated disinformation.

title: Securing LLMs In The Wild: Privacy And Security Challenges At The Edge
authors: Ren-Yi Huang, Mingchen Li, Dumindu Samaraweera, Morris Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly moving from research settings into the wild, deployed on enterprise infrastructure, personal devices, and edge platforms. While cloud deployments offer scalable compute, concerns over data sovereignty, compliance, latency, and third-party dependence are driving organizations toward edge and on-premise LLMs. This shift introduces new security and privacy challenges: limited compute and memory force aggressive optimizations, including quantization, pruning, model partitioning, and parameter-efficient adaptation, each of which can introduce vulnerabilities and reshape the threat landscape. We describe this tension as the Security-Efficiency Paradox, mechanisms that improve efficiency may weaken robustness, expose new attack surfaces, or increase privacy risks. We examine how compression can degrade safety alignment, how partitioned inference enables reconstruction attacks, and how continuous local adaptation may cause privacy leakage and model drift. To analyze these risks, we introduce a deployment-centric taxonomy organized around three architectural constraints: the Memory Wall, the Quadratic Wall, and the Compute Wall. We derive a unified constraint model that quantifies when unsafe optimizations become unavoidable, linking each wall to specific attack surfaces. Building on this model, we propose the Secure Operational Efficiency Score (SOES), a holistic metric balancing task accuracy, jailbreak resistance, and privacy against energy, memory, and latency, enabling practitioners to configure edge LLMs under real-world hardware limits. We further present a practical decision procedure and targeted mitigations for each optimization-induced vulnerability. Together, these contributions provide a co-designed framework for jointly evaluating security, privacy, and efficiency, laying a foundation for securing edge-native intelligent systems.
tldr: This paper discusses security and privacy challenges of deploying LLMs on edge devices, focusing on the trade-off between efficiency and robustness.
motivation: As LLMs move to edge and on-premise deployments, new security and privacy vulnerabilities arise due to hardware constraints and aggressive optimizations.
method: The authors introduce a deployment-centric taxonomy (Memory, Quadratic, Compute Walls) and a unified constraint model, then propose the Secure Operational Efficiency Score (SOES) and a decision procedure for configuring edge LLMs.
result: They identify specific attack surfaces linked to each constraint wall and provide targeted mitigations for optimization-induced vulnerabilities.
conclusion: The paper provides a co-designed framework for jointly evaluating security, privacy, and efficiency, laying a foundation for securing edge-native intelligent systems.

title: Efficient And Privacy Aware Edge Cloud Collaborative Inference For Large Language Models
authors: Yi Li, Chen Li, Jiexiong Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-device LLM inference faces a trilemma of response latency, limited hardware resources and user privacy. Full cloud inference delivers strong computing power but exposes user prompts and dialogue data, while standalone on-device inference is unfeasible for most consumer and embedded edge devices. This paper presents a privacy-centric edge-cloud collaborative LLM inference framework built on endpoint-authenticated KV cache. Local endpoints handle input preprocessing, embedding computation, adaptive feature optimization, KV cache authentication, speculative decoding and low-dimensional model head calculation, while the cloud conducts authenticated decoder inference, KV cache management, token verification and high-dimensional vocabulary projection. Endpoints fuse partial outputs, apply language-adaptive masking and sample target tokens. All transmitted data and truncated logits are quantized and AES-GCM encrypted for privacy, with core lightweight modules, draft parameters and cache access policies kept local to avoid leakage. The framework supports heterogeneous devices including CPU-only, GPU-equipped and embedded devices via optimized streaming, batching and quantized ONNX deployment. Evaluations demonstrate that the framework reduces per-token latency by up to 46.1\% and downlink payloads by up to 67.4\% over baseline split inference, retaining comparable performance to full cloud inference.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving edge-cloud collaborative inference framework for large language models using authenticated KV cache and encryption.
motivation: On-device LLM inference faces a trilemma of latency, resource constraints, and privacy; full cloud inference exposes user data.
method: The framework splits computation between local endpoints (input preprocessing, embedding, speculative decoding) and cloud (authenticated decoder inference, KV cache management), with AES-GCM encryption and quantization for privacy.
result: The framework reduces per-token latency by up to 46.1% and downlink payloads by up to 67.4% over baseline split inference, with comparable performance to full cloud inference.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively balances efficiency and privacy for LLM inference on heterogeneous edge devices.

title: Ai In Cyberpsychology: A Systematic Literature Review Of Cybersecurity Enhancement By Using Ai For Analyzing Psychology Of Victims, Attackers, And Defenders
authors: Georg Thamer Francis, Malek Malkawi, Sevim Ey\"upo\u{g}lu, Reda Alhajj, Selim Akyoku\c{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems, networks, and data from digital attacks. Cyberpsychology (CPSY) is defined as the use of psychology to enhance cybersecurity applications. Since the early 2010s, the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has increasingly integrated with CPSY, leveraging advanced data analysis to decode the distinct personality traits and behavioral patterns of victims, attackers, and defenders. In this systematic literature review (SLR), we carefully analyze 34 collected research studies of AI usage in cyberpsychology (AI-CPSY) using the preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) methodology. The review presents a comprehensive taxonomy of the cyber-security applications, the AI methodologies used, and the psychological concepts employed across the studies . We sort the research studies into four cybersecurity applications: Anomaly Detection (AD), Vulnerability Risk Prediction (VRP), Security Awareness Training (SAT), and Authentication/Identity Verification (AIV). Within each application area, studies are further sorted according to the AI method used including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning (RL). Furthermore, the review identifies the most commonly utilized psychological concepts, quantify the datasets used in the field, and present their current implementation and deployment status. At last, it detect research gaps, present open challenges, and deduce the trending and most effective and emerging methodologies used across the AI-CPSY landscape.
tldr: A systematic literature review on the use of AI to analyze psychology of victims, attackers, and defenders for cybersecurity enhancement.
motivation: To understand how AI can be integrated with cyberpsychology to improve cybersecurity by analyzing human behavior.
method: Conducted a systematic literature review using PRISMA methodology, analyzing 34 studies and categorizing them by cybersecurity application and AI method.
result: Identified four main cybersecurity applications (Anomaly Detection, Vulnerability Risk Prediction, Security Awareness Training, Authentication/Identity Verification) and various AI methods used.
conclusion: The field of AI-cyberpsychology is emerging with potential, but faces challenges such as limited datasets and deployment gaps.

title: Privacy Preserving Recommender Systems Balancing Personalization With Privacy
authors: Venkata Suresh Gummadilli Ranjeet K Jha
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized recommendation systems are central to modern e-commerce and retail platforms, but they typically rely on centralized storage of detailed user interaction data, creating significant privacy and regulatory challenges. With increasing requirements from regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, and CPRA, organizations must develop recommendation systems that preserve user privacy without substantially degrading recommendation quality. This work presents and evaluates a privacy-preserving recommendation framework that combines federated learning, differential privacy, cohort-level modeling, and privacy-aware intelligent agents. The framework keeps raw user data decentralized while introducing mathematically bounded noise to model updates. Experiments were conducted on synthetic retail datasets that emulate customer clickstream and purchase behavior. Recommendation quality was evaluated using Click-Through Rate (CTR), Precision@K, Recall@K, and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG@K) across multiple differential privacy budgets. We evaluate matrix factorization, neural collaborative filtering, and GRU4Rec under varying privacy constraints and analyze the trade-off between privacy and utility. An interactive Streamlit dashboard was developed to visualize recommendation performance, ranking stability, privacy-utility trade-offs, and fairness metrics. Results show that the proposed framework maintains competitive recommendation quality at moderate privacy budgets (approximately [MATH]), demonstrating that strong privacy guarantees can be achieved with limited impact on recommendation effectiveness. This work provides a practical framework for deploying privacy-preserving recommendation systems that balance personalization, regulatory compliance, and business objectives, offering a scalable approach for next-generation AI-driven retail platforms.
tldr: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving recommendation framework using federated learning and differential privacy, evaluated on synthetic retail datasets.
motivation: Personalized recommendation systems rely on centralized user data, raising privacy concerns and regulatory challenges under GDPR, CCPA, etc.
method: The framework combines federated learning, differential privacy, cohort-level modeling, and privacy-aware agents; experiments use matrix factorization, neural collaborative filtering, and GRU4Rec on synthetic data.
result: At moderate privacy budgets, the framework maintains competitive recommendation quality (CTR, Precision@K, Recall@K, NDCG@K) with limited impact on effectiveness.
conclusion: Strong privacy guarantees can be achieved with acceptable trade-offs in recommendation quality, offering a scalable approach for privacy-preserving retail platforms.

title: Adversarial Prompting Framework For Ai Safety Assessment
authors: Yash Bhatnagar, Kunal Banerjee, Anirban Chatterjee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), especially Generative AI (GenAI), adoption has increased in industries significantly in recent years. However, the use of these models may also expose systems to new forms of cyberattacks by different malicious actors -- adversarial prompt attack (APA) being one of the most prominent examples of such threats. This paper presents the implementation of an Adversarial Prompting Framework (APF) for a comprehensive assessment of AI safety. The framework systematically evaluates the resilience of the AI model through the generation of structured adversarial prompts at multiple sophistication levels, from direct harmful requests to advanced encoding-based attacks. Our implementation demonstrates the practical application of this methodology in enterprise environments, providing automated testing capabilities with quantitative security assessment metrics. The results indicate significant variations in the model vulnerabilities across different attack vectors, with encoded prompts presenting the highest success rates in bypassing safety mechanisms.
tldr: This paper presents an adversarial prompting framework for assessing the safety of generative AI models against various attack levels.
motivation: The increasing adoption of generative AI in industry exposes systems to new cyber threats, particularly adversarial prompt attacks, necessitating a systematic safety assessment methodology.
method: The framework generates structured adversarial prompts at multiple sophistication levels, from direct harmful requests to encoding-based attacks, and evaluates model resilience in enterprise environments.

tldr: This paper uses physics-informed neural networks to solve saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, specifically for above-threshold ionization.
motivation: Solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that is efficient and accurate.
method: An unsupervised physics-informed neural network (PINN) is designed to solve the saddle-point equations governing direct above-threshold ionization within the strong-field approximation.
result: The PINN successfully reproduces known saddle-point structures and provides accurate solutions for tailored fields.
conclusion: Physics-informed neural networks offer a viable alternative for solving saddle-point equations in strong-field physics, with potential for extension to more complex scenarios.

title: Surface Phase Separation In A Confined Space
authors: Daoning Wu And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Daoning Wu and Jie Lin

Biomolecular condensates frequently form near surfaces, including lipid membranes. However, the effect of a surface on phase separation within a cell, a confined system, remains elusive. In this work, we study surface phase separation under the constraint of a finite number of molecules in a confine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033007] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surface phase separation in confined spaces, relevant to biophysics and soft matter, but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates often form near surfaces, but the effect of confinement on phase separation is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically model surface phase separation under finite molecule number constraints in a confined geometry.
result: They find that confinement alters phase behavior, leading to surface-induced phase separation with distinct scaling laws.
conclusion: Surface phase separation in confined spaces is a distinct phenomenon that may be relevant to cellular organization.

title: Shear Jamming Transition In Alternating Shear Rotation For Frictional And Frictionless Suspensions
authors: Pappu Acharya And Martin Trulsson
abstract:
Author(s): Pappu Acharya and Martin Trulsson

Alternating shear rotations in dense suspensions have recently shown the ability to reduce both viscosity and dissipation per strain (at a fixed global shear rate). Here, we study alternating shear rotations, with extensive numerical simulations, at various angles and up to their corresponding jammi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033013] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shear jamming transitions in dense suspensions under alternating shear rotations, focusing on rheological properties.
motivation: Understanding jamming transitions in suspensions is important for material processing, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Extensive numerical simulations of frictional and frictionless suspensions under alternating shear rotations at various angles.
result: Alternating shear rotations can reduce viscosity and dissipation per strain, and the jamming transition depends on the rotation angle.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into shear jamming but are purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding anisotropy in silica films can inform better coating design.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films, including anisotropy and its response to heat treatment.
result: They discover hidden anisotropy in silica films that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating performance.
conclusion: The findings guide strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and enable fluorescence imaging at the atomic scale for studying molecules and their reactions.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a nanoscale optical antenna at the tip apex to confine the electromagnetic field, achieving superresolution.
result: Demonstrates atomic-scale spatial resolution in fluorescence imaging, revealing electronic and vibronic properties of individual molecules.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for submolecular imaging and understanding molecular structures and reactions.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic behavior at the boundary between localized and itinerant 5f electrons.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: The review summarizes the current understanding of pressure-induced changes in electronic structure, bonding, and phase transitions in these materials.
conclusion: High-pressure studies reveal complex behavior in transplutonium compounds, but the work is primarily materials science and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and related physics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This Nobel lecture describes Boltzmann machines, a type of neural network for unsupervised learning.
motivation: To explain the concept and training of Boltzmann machines, which are foundational in machine learning.
method: The lecture reviews the architecture, energy-based model, and contrastive divergence algorithm for training Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines can learn complex probability distributions and generate new data samples.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines are a powerful tool for unsupervised learning, though they are not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers three real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review techniques that provide direct real-space access.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can reveal atomic-scale details of disorder in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods are powerful for characterizing disorder, and combining them yields more comprehensive insights.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the quantum mechanical phenomena underlying low-energy nuclear reactions in stars.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but many reactions occur at very low energies with small rates, making direct measurement difficult.
method: The authors summarize the state-of-the-art theory of low-energy nuclear reactions, focusing on quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of theoretical approaches and new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.
conclusion: Quantum mechanical effects dominate low-energy nuclear reactions, and further theoretical and experimental advances are needed to fully understand stellar nucleosynthesis.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improved uncertainties.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with updated uncertainties compared to previous editions.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical work across physics and chemistry.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering collective behaviors and applications in biology and robotics.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment of active units with their velocity leads to novel collective phenomena.
method: Unified mathematical and conceptual framework, review of existing models.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors like orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with potential for smart materials and robotics.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep-tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in scattering tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advances in multimodal approaches.

title: Machine-learning-enabled Solvent Engineering For Uniform Quantum Dot Packing In Efficient And Stable Quantum-dot Light-emitting Diodes
authors: Beomsoo Chun, Byong Jae Kim, Hyeongjin Kim, Jeong Han Song, Yeongsik Kim, Jaehoon Lim And Jeonghun Kwak
abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) offer size-tunable optoelectronic properties and solution processability, yet achieving uniformly packed emissive layers remains a bottleneck for high-performance quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Here, we report a machine learning -guided solvent optimization strategy to produce homogeneous QD films. Five representative solvent parameters are evaluated, and multiple regression models are trained against film uniformity derived from atomic force microscopy. Among them, support vector regression provides the highest predictive accuracy for film homogeneity. Guided by these predictions, we formulate a mixed solvent that closely matches the target profile, yielding superior packing homogeneity, which is confirmed by grazing-incidence small-angle x-ray scattering.
